PROGRAM: swarm-context-graph (program-triage-2026-10-17; pins in triage-2026-10-17/PINS.txt; shard requirements/swarm-context-graph-requirements.md; dossier triage/swarm-context-graph-dossier.md; audit requirements/RELEASE-CLAIMS-AUDIT.md).

STATEMENT: When result.observations carries any row that is not a fresh observed value — replayed===true, or freshness==='reused', or degraded===true, or a status outside the pin's observed-value set {observed, null} (including any unknown word) — the RF reader adapter shall project coverage 'partial' and a statusTone other than 'success', with one note naming the row count, the reused/replayed count and the verbatim status words; all-fresh rows, observations [] or absent keep today's output byte-identical.

RATIONALE: Dossier G5 (CONFIRMED-GAP observations-rows-reused-not-current): SCG-R024 (01-PRODUCT-AND-REQUIREMENTS.md:37@8a8b83e4d), ADR-SCG-008 (09-ADRS-AND-DECISIONS.md:26-27), 11-SKILL-AND-LX-DELIVERY.md:13 (freshness witnesses, not model conjecture), 04-CLI-AND-SCHEMAS.md:94 (replayed = host projection of reuse; freshness = host witness). The key rides every pinned render (render_service.py:1513@8a8b83e4d); pin vocabulary status observed|missing|null|suppressed|invalid|timeout|nonzero|truncated|denied, freshness captured_at_render|reused, replayed and degraded booleans (context.render.schema.json:1071-1082,:1112-1152@8a8b83e4d; observed-value statuses domain/observation.py:100). Pi computes clean = live && !flagged && !overBudget without reading rows (reactivefiber-observer.ts:187-198@9df9a03) and the projection stamps freshness 'current' from connection state (observation.ts:588) — a reused or denied row on an ok, zero-error envelope reads complete/success/current today; the one gap that mislabels evidence at the pin, hence P0. Correction carried: the program's reused/stale_inputs status words (03-LOW-LEVEL-DESIGN.md:44) are a planned migration, not the pin's enum.

ACCEPTANCE: ["RED on 9df9a03, it.each over three rows on an otherwise clean rf-cli envelope: (a) {observation_id:'rfl_…', lens_key:'beads.current', value_digest:'sha256:…', status:'observed', code:null, freshness:'reused', replayed:true, required:true, degraded:false, persisted:true}; (b) {…, status:'denied', code:'RF_OBSERVATION_DENIED', freshness:'captured_at_render', replayed:false, degraded:true}; (c) {…, status:'stale_inputs', freshness:'captured_at_render', replayed:false, degraded:false} — each asserts coverage==='partial', statusTone!=='success', a note matching /observations: 1 row/ naming reused/replayed for (a) and the verbatim status word for (b),(c); HEAD projects complete/success for all three.", "Positive controls: observations [], absent, and one row {status:'observed', freshness:'captured_at_render', replayed:false, degraded:false} leave the clean R1 expectation toStrictEqual unchanged except, for the fresh row, one added note 'observations: 1 row, 0 reused'.", "Contradiction fences (schema :1140,:1144): replayed:true with freshness 'captured_at_render', replayed:false with freshness 'reused', degraded:true with status 'observed' → refused 'validation'; a row missing status/freshness/replayed or a non-array observations → 'validation' (observer) / 'transport' (provider).", "Projection effect: after ObservationProjection.refresh the node's completeness==='partial'; the adapter writes no projection freshness field (freshness semantics stay projection-owned; the note is the row-level witness).", 'Gate: default gate (fixture keys from R11).']

STATEMENT: The committing rf invocation path shall capture and journal the stderr receipt line's operation_id before any deadline/overflow kill, and shall never SIGKILL a committing render without a subsequent operation-id reconcile; the no-commit preview's stderr discard and SIGTERM-SIGKILL(500 ms) custody remain byte-unchanged. Gate artifact: a committing rf capability in Pi (wb-x32, the R5 gate) plus a resolvable receipt id — rf operation show (FOC-06-c/rfc-mq7k6.15) or context history/show carrying operation_id (FOC-06-e/rfc-mq7k6.26); the producer's stderr receipt line itself is already on rf main at the pin (STORE-TXN-A27, FOC/BEADS-2026-10-16.md:100@8a8b83e4d).

RATIONALE: Dossier §1.4 (UNDETERMINED, new this wave, rf-stderr-receipt-line-capture): Pi counts stderr bytes and discards content (providers/reactivefiber.ts:107-110@9df9a03) and kills on deadline (:88-95,98) — correct for the --no-commit leaf but it would discard the only pre-stdout operation identity of a committing render; 'For callers timing out, operation show recovers the outcome from the journal, not from stdout files' (FOC/03:48@8a8b83e4d). Pi's own report noted the stream split (report line 21@0e6e88345).

STATEMENT: Any future committing rf capability shall register with a non-read effectClass, pass a stable --idempotency-key on the render argv, and on any committed or unknown outcome reconcile via rf operation show instead of retrying — never directing or performing a retry after a diagnostic with metadata.committed=true or an authoritative committed receipt (FOC/03:40@8a8b83e4d), and never treating not-found/stdout absence as proof of no commit (FOC/03:34,48@8a8b83e4d). Gate artifact (conjoint): rf operation show registered leaf (FOC-06-c/rfc-mq7k6.15) + --idempotency-key on context render (FOC-06-d2/rfc-mq7k6.17, per ruling R-14) + FOC-ADR-03 (rfc-mq7k6.23) landed in an installed rf (0 hits in cli/registry.py and cli/parser.py at 8a8b83e4d, re-measured), conjoined with wb-x32 resolving to a committing render.

RATIONALE: Dossier §1.2 (UNDETERMINED, rf-receipt-consumption-on-committed-interop): Pi has no committing rf path today (sole argv --no-commit at providers/reactivefiber.ts:79@9df9a03; all 10 effectClass sites read), and a committing capability built to today's provider pattern would blind-kill a render whose commit may already be durable (FOC/00:25: commit visible 6.5-13.6 s before stdout in 21/21 pairs). Generic uncertain-effect machinery exists at capability-registry.ts:418@9df9a03.

ACCEPTANCE: ["A registration test beside test/workbench-provider-lifecycle.test.ts asserts the committing descriptor's effectClass != read and its argv carries --idempotency-key <stable key>.", 'On timeout/kill/unknown outcome the invoke path surfaces CapabilityError(uncertain-effect) and the runtime issues no second invocation (exactly one spawn asserted).', 'Outcome resolution reads rf operation show receipt states (not_found/in_progress/committed/refused_before_commit/indeterminate, FOC/03:34@8a8b83e4d); not_found while an attempt may be in flight does not conclude effect-absent.', "Negative guards: the read-only preview registrations (providers/reactivefiber.ts:68,:142@9df9a03) stay byte-stable; the preview's SIGTERM-SIGKILL(500 ms) custody is never reused for the committing call; NATIVE_GRANTS.reactivefiber stays read-scoped for the preview (hosts/local-detached.ts:337@9df9a03) and the committing capability needs a new write grant."]

title: W16-C: pure bounded workflow_catalog and workflow_inspect reply builders over the capability registry policy surface (filter/limit/cursor pagination, exact discover:/inspect: grant ACL, compact bounded sanitized JSON, never implicit invocation); Pi tool registration excluded
description:
Gap (groomed at rig HEAD 1fc74f0, branch workbench/implementation-program): wb-69g (W16) spans workflow_catalog/inspect/validate/execute/observe/control/compare, but its only children cover workflow_control decisions (wb-69g.1) and the workflow_observe reply builder (wb-752.2). Nothing covers the catalog/inspect reply half, and docs/workbench/15 W16 acceptance is "compact bounded result and ACL".

Scope (atomic, pure, hot-file free): a new pure module (suggested src/workbench/tool-replies.ts or sibling-consistent location) exporting buildWorkflowCatalogReply(registrySnapshot, grants, {filter?, limit?, cursor?}) and buildWorkflowInspectReply(registrySnapshot, grants, target, view?) that return compact bounded sanitized JSON reply objects for the Pi tools, plus a red-first vitest. ACL is exact-string and deny-by-default: a capability id without discover:<capabilityId> in the grant set is absent from the catalog reply (absent, not an error row); an inspect reply requires inspect:<capabilityId> AND an advertised, implemented inspect mode, else an explicit typed unavailable. Cursor pagination is stable; a byte cap truncates with a visible marker and offered-vs-returned counts; every string field routes through the shared sanitizers in src/workbench/redaction.ts. The builders perform no invocation and no RPC.

Out of scope: Pi tool registration in src/index.ts (parent slice), observation-backed inspect views (wb-752.2 owns workflow_observe), workflow_validate/execute/control/compare, and ALL W17 hot-reservation files (src/workbench/designer.ts, test/workbench-designer.test.ts, test/workbench-pi-designer.test.ts, workflow_compare surfacing in src/index.ts).
acceptance_criteria:
Red-first: the new vitest fails before the builder module exists. Base 1fc74f0 or later. All quotes are from docs/workbench in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program).

A1. Catalog shape and pagination. buildWorkflowCatalogReply honors filter/limit/cursor with a stable cursor, enforces a byte cap with a visible truncation marker and offered-vs-returned counts, and returns compact structured JSON only. Quote docs/workbench/11-designer-and-operator.md section "First public Pi tools (proposed)": "workflow_catalog(filter?,limit?,cursor?): saved script sources, MechanicalWorkflows entrypoints, available SDK capabilities and contract references." Quote same section: "Use compact structured schema, discover more capability detail on demand; do not insert all SDK method signatures into every Pi prompt."

A2. ACL exact-string, deny-by-default. A capability whose id lacks discover:<capabilityId> in the grant set is absent from the catalog reply; inspect requires inspect:<capabilityId> plus an advertised, implemented inspect mode, else a typed explicit unavailable; discovery never implies invoke. Quote docs/workbench/06-capability-registry.md section "Current experimental policy surface": "Catalog discovery independently requires exact `discover:<capabilityId>`. Optional provider inspection requires `inspect:<capabilityId>` and an advertised, implemented inspect mode." Quote same section: "Registered descriptors do not grant access." Quote docs/workbench/15-implementation-program.md section "Work breakdown and dependencies" W16 row acceptance: "compact bounded result and ACL".

A3. Inspect never invokes. buildWorkflowInspectReply is pure over its inputs, performs no invocation and no RPC; unknown target or view yields a typed explicit error reply, never a guess. Quote docs/workbench/11-designer-and-operator.md section "First public Pi tools (proposed)": "workflow_inspect(target,view?): definition/source, static projection, native reference/evidence, operation details, never implicit invocation."

A4. Sanitization and falsifiers. Every string field routes through the shared sanitizers in src/workbench/redaction.ts (invariant); offline falsifiers: an empty grant set yields zero catalog rows; a crafted capability title containing an ESC control character is sanitized in the reply; a cursor past the end returns an empty page, not an error; an oversized snapshot triggers the visible truncation marker.

title: W15-B/VC-5: pure timeline lane model over observed source intervals and native-confirmed ownership/grouping edges (lanes per owner or provider, open intervals stay open, measured concurrency, zoom/pan cell math, clock and gap notes); inspector wiring excluded
description:
Gap (measured at rig HEAD 1fc74f0, branch workbench/implementation-program): src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts:177-191 renders the timeline view as one flat line per viewport node: a bar `(ascii?'#':'━').repeat(Math.max(1,Math.min(20,Math.floor(duration/1000*state.zoom)-state.pan)))` computed only when node.interval has both startedAt and endedAt, otherwise the literal 'timing unavailable (no complete source interval)', closed by the constant 'Waiting/blocked/executing lanes unavailable without producer interval kinds.' No lane grouping exists (the furnace-confirmed Run->Attempt ownership edges that wb-752.1 landed at e797a84 are never consulted by the timeline), no concurrency is measured, an open interval (startedAt without endedAt, which ObservationProjection keeps as-is, test/workbench-observation.test.ts:128) is reported as unavailable instead of open, and the zoom/pan arithmetic lives untested inside the renderer (test/workbench-inspector.test.ts:103 only checks that pan changes the line). docs/workbench/10 § "Four views" (Timeline) requires "relative interval lanes grouped by owner/phase/provider, zoom and horizontal pan, observed waiting/executing/blocked periods and concurrency. Never infer exact timing from text or assume clocks agree; note uncertain clocks or event gaps." ObservationProjection already exposes every read needed: window({scope,invocationId,offset,limit}) -> {nodes,total,revision} with ObservedNode.interval {startedAt,endedAt?} (src/workbench/observation.ts:448), relations({scope,to,limit}) returning incoming typed edges with provenance (:397) and relationRevision() (:467). wb-6ze.1 (in progress) owns workflow-inspector.ts for the overview tree and graph fan-out and leaves the timeline branch untouched; wb-6ze.2 adds ancestor counts in observation.ts; wb-6ze.4 ranks bottlenecks and estimates a critical path. None of them computes lanes, concurrency or the zoom/pan window.

Scope (atomic, pure, hot-file free): ONE new source file src/workbench/timeline.ts and ONE new test file test/workbench-timeline.test.ts; register and wire nothing; do not edit src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts (wb-6ze.1 in flight), src/workbench/observation.ts (wb-6ze.2), src/workbench/designer.ts (reserved 07:00Z), src/index.ts or src/ui/workflow-dialog.ts.

• export const TIMELINE_CONTRACT = 'workbench.timeline/v1'; export type TimelineReader = Pick<ObservationProjection,'window'|'relations'|'relationRevision'>.
• export interface TimelineRequest { scope: ObservationScope; invocationId: string; offset: number; limit: number (1..100, the window cap); zoom: number (safe integer 1..8, cells per second); pan: number (safe integer >= 0, cells); columns: number (safe integer 8..200, bar cells); maxLanes?: number (1..64, default 16); maxRowsPerLane?: number (1..100, default 40); relationLimit?: number (1..100, default 40) }. Invalid values throw CapabilityError('validation') before any reader call.
• export function buildTimelineLanes(reader: TimelineReader, request: TimelineRequest): TimelineModel — pure, synchronous, deterministic (no Date.now, Math.random, process or environment reads; every timestamp comes from reader rows), calls reader.window exactly once and reader.relations at most once per returned node with {scope, to: node.key, limit: relationLimit}; never calls ingest/refresh/relate/markStale or any provider; returns a deeply frozen plain object that survives JSON round-trip losslessly.
• TimelineModel { contract; revision; topologyRevision; origin: { startedAt: string; basis: 'earliest-observed-start' } | { startedAt: null; basis: 'none' }; span: { ms: number | null; complete: boolean }; lanes: readonly TimelineLane[]; concurrency: { maxMeasured: number; basis: 'source-intervals-only'; countsOpenIntervals: true }; notes: readonly TimelineNote[]; truncated: { lanes: boolean; rows: boolean; relations: boolean; window: boolean } }.
• TimelineLane { key: string; label: string; basis: 'ownership' | 'grouping' | 'provider'; confirmed: boolean; rows: readonly TimelineRow[] }. Lane assignment per row: an incoming 'ownership' edge from a node in the same scope -> lane key = that parent's key, basis 'ownership'; else an incoming 'grouping' edge -> that parent's key, basis 'grouping'; else lane key `provider:${nativeRef.provider}`, basis 'provider'. When several parents of the chosen kind qualify, the lexicographically smallest parent key wins and note 'multiple-parents' is added; 'dependency', 'causation' and 'hypothesis' edges never assign a lane or alter timing. confirmed is true only when every edge used for the lane carries provenance.nativeConfirmationRef. Lane label is the parent's presentation.title (redactWorkbenchText then stripUnsafeText, max 80) when the parent is inside the window, else the sanitized parent key, else the provider name.
• TimelineRow { key; nativeRef; title (sanitized, max 80); tone: Presentation['statusTone']; freshness; timing: { kind: 'closed'; startedAt; endedAt; durationMs } | { kind: 'open'; startedAt } | { kind: 'unavailable'; reason: 'no-source-interval' }; bar: { offsetCells; lengthCells; clippedLeft; clippedRight; openEnded } | null }. No field named elapsedMs, estimatedEndedAt or progressPercent exists anywhere in the model.
• Ordering: lanes by earliest row startedAt then key; rows inside a lane by startedAt then key; rows without an interval last, by key. Rows beyond maxRowsPerLane and lanes beyond maxLanes are dropped with truncated.rows / truncated.lanes true; truncated.window is total > offset + returned; truncated.relations is true when any relations page returned exactly relationLimit rows.
• Bar math: origin = earliest startedAt over rows with a parsable interval; offsetCells = floor((startedAt - origin)/1000 * zoom) - pan; closed lengthCells = max(1, floor(durationMs/1000 * zoom)); open bars extend to the right edge with openEnded true; bars are clipped to [0, columns) with clippedLeft/clippedRight flags; a bar entirely outside the viewport becomes bar null and note 'rows-outside-viewport' is added. Unparsable timestamps produce timing 'unavailable' (never a throw: the projection already validated dates).
• Concurrency: sweep over interval boundaries of the returned rows: a closed interval counts on [startedAt, endedAt), an open interval counts from startedAt to the latest known boundary; maxMeasured is the maximum simultaneous count; rows without intervals never count.
• Notes (frozen vocabulary, each at most once): 'clocks-may-differ' (present whenever intervals come from more than one nativeRef.provider), 'open-intervals-present', 'intervals-missing' (carries a count), 'stale-rows-present', 'window-partial', 'relation-page-full', 'multiple-parents', 'rows-outside-viewport', 'phase-kinds-unavailable' (always present: Interval carries no waiting/executing/blocked kinds, so lanes show source intervals only).

Files: src/workbench/timeline.ts (new), test/workbench-timeline.test.ts (new). Specs: docs/workbench/10 (Four views; Rendering pipeline; Scalability targets), docs/workbench/09 (Relationships are typed and provenanced; Freshness and ambiguity; Aggregates and profiling), docs/workbench/13 (Observation projection; Key validations), docs/workbench/12 (Input and output hardening), docs/workbench/02 WB-027/WB-029/WB-030, docs/workbench/16 § New paths (ui/timeline.ts).

title: W13/VC-5: Claude session reader adapter projects agent-call, session and tool-use NativeSnapshots with observed ownership, causation and grouping edges from ClaudeNativeObservation (bounded, redacted, no invented ids); Pi observer wiring excluded
description:
Gap: `grep -rln NativeSnapshot src` at rig ad3cf6e returns only src/workbench/observation.ts and src/workbench/furnace-observer.ts. Claude is the one provider that has produced real native sessions (VC-1 measured) yet it has no reader adapter. src/index.ts:2676 (hot) consumes createClaudeObserver and ingests ONE flat 'claude.stream' event per sampled ClaudeNativeObservation whose source key flips from {pi-workflow, agent-call, `${task.id}:${index}`} before init to {claude-agent-sdk, session, sessionId} after init, with no relation between the two keys and no tool-use nodes at all; ClaudeNativeObservation.tools (toolUseId/name/state) never reaches the projection. The inspector therefore shows Claude work as disconnected flat rows: no agent-call -> session link and no session -> tool-use children, so wb-6ze.1's nested tree and wb-6ze.2's aggregates have nothing to nest for the provider that actually runs. docs/workbench/09 § Reader adapters lists Claude first ("SDK message events from sessions controlled by Workbench") and § Derived view indexes requires "allow local temporary ID before native assignment; rekey safely and preserve selection".

Scope (atomic, additive, hot-file free): ONE new source file src/workbench/claude-topology.ts and ONE new test file test/workbench-claude-topology.test.ts; register and wire nothing.

- export type ClaudeObservedRelation = Parameters<ObservationProjection['relate']>[0];
- export interface ClaudeTopologyInput { call: ClaudeCallIdentity; snapshot: ClaudeNativeObservation; scope: ObservationScope; invocationId: string; observedAt: string; sequence: number; definitionDigest?: string; subjectBasis?: string }
- export interface ClaudeProjectionTopology { snapshots: NativeSnapshot[]; relations: ClaudeObservedRelation[]; truncated: boolean }
- export function projectClaudeTopology(input: ClaudeTopologyInput): ClaudeProjectionTopology — pure, synchronous, deterministic (no Date.now or Math.random; observedAt and sequence come from the caller), frozen result.
  • Agent-call snapshot ALWAYS: source {provider:'pi-workflow', type:'agent-call', id:`${invocationId}:${call.index}`} (the same key shape src/index.ts:2680 uses before init so existing rows keep their key); node {title: call.label through redactWorkbenchText then stripUnsafeText, max 120 chars; type:'agent'; statusText: snapshot.terminal ?? 'observed-running'; statusTone: succeeded->success, failed->failure, cancelled/observation_lost->unknown, live->active}; kind 'claude.call'; trace {invocationId}; sequence; capturedAt and observedAt = input.observedAt; coverage 'partial' (the observer samples at most 64 snapshots per call); definitionDigest and subjectBasis passed through when supplied.
  • Session snapshot ONLY when snapshot.sessionId is a non-empty string: source {provider:'claude-agent-sdk', type:'session', id: sessionId}; node type 'agent', title `${label} · session`, same status mapping; kind 'claude.session'; evidenceRefs [`claude-message:${lastMessageId}`] only when lastMessageId exists; coverage 'unknown' when snapshot.freshness === 'unknown' else 'partial'. Never synthesize a session id from the agent id, pid, label or index.
  • One tool-use snapshot per snapshot.tools entry (<= 16 by construction), only when a session snapshot exists (a tool_use block is observed inside the session's native messages): source {provider:'claude-agent-sdk', type:'tool-use', id: toolUseId}; node {title: sanitized name, max 80; type:'sdk-operation'; statusText: the literal state ('started'|'completed'|'refused'|'failed'); statusTone: started->active, completed->success, failed->failure, refused->failure}; kind 'claude.tool-use'; trace {invocationId}.
  • Relations: ownership agent-call -> session with provenance {source:'pi-workflow', observedAt, nativeConfirmationRef: sessionId} (the workflow host that launched query() owns exactly that session; the SDK-reported session_id is the confirmation, satisfying the relate() rule at observation.ts:385 that provenance.source === from.provider and nativeConfirmationRef is present). Per tool-use: causation session -> tool-use with provenance {source:'claude-observer', observedAt, nativeConfirmationRef: toolUseId} AND grouping session -> tool-use with provenance {source:'claude-observer', observedAt} (display nesting; wb-6ze.1 nests on grouping/ownership only). No dependency or hypothesis edge is ever emitted; no edge references a node absent from `snapshots`.
  • truncated = snapshot.toolsTruncated; evicted tools are never invented.

Out of scope: editing src/index.ts (hot; the observer callback at :2676 is the parent's wiring point), src/workbench/claude-host.ts, src/workbench/claude-transcript.ts, src/workflow/progress.ts, src/workbench/redaction.ts (import only), src/workbench/observation.ts (wb-6ze.2 edits it additively; this bead adds no projection API); transcript bodies, token counts, Pi tool output. A1. docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md section "Reader adapters": "Claude: SDK message events from sessions controlled by Workbench; external Claude sessions may be unobservable unless records are available." and "Reader adapter returns snapshot {nativeRef, capturedAt, observedAt, sourceRevision?, coverage?, nativePayloadRef} and optional change stream with cursor." -> for a snapshot with sessionId 'sess-1', lastMessageId 'm-9' and two tools, projectClaudeTopology returns exactly 4 snapshots (agent-call, session, 2 tool-use), each with source, scope, capturedAt, observedAt, sequence, coverage, node, kind and trace set; the session snapshot's evidenceRefs deep-equal ['claude-message:m-9']; no snapshot carries nativePayloadRef or transcript text.

A2. docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md section "Derived view indexes": "Use stable keys by provider+native identity, but allow local temporary ID before native assignment; rekey safely and preserve selection." -> a pre-init snapshot (no sessionId) yields exactly one snapshot whose source is {provider:'pi-workflow', type:'agent-call', id:'<invocationId>:<index>'} and zero relations; the post-init snapshot for the same call yields the SAME agent-call source plus the session snapshot and an ownership edge from that agent-call key to the session key; applying both in order to a default ObservationProjection leaves window({scope, invocationId, offset:0, limit:50}).total equal to the number of distinct keys (no duplicate agent-call row) and indexOf for the agent-call key unchanged.

A6. docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md section "Acceptance/negative controls" item 2: "Replay duplicate/out-of-order events; no double count or status regression." -> applying projection.refresh over the topology for sequence 2 (terminal 'succeeded') and then over the topology for sequence 1 (live) returns 'out-of-order' for every sequence-1 snapshot and the session node's statusText remains 'succeeded'; applying the same sequence twice never increases stats().nodes or stats().edges.

A7. docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md section "Acceptance/negative controls" item 10: "Large/secret payload does not leak into Pi tool result or screen by default." and docs/workbench/04-claude-agent-sdk-executor.md section "Streaming and progress": "Avoid printing secrets or tool payloads in overview." -> a call.label of 'deploy \u001b[31mBearer abc123\\u202E' and a tool name containing 'api_key=xyz' produce titles with no control or bidi characters and with the credential replaced by the marker redactWorkbenchText emits; JSON.stringify(result) contains neither 'abc123' nor 'xyz'; titles are at most 120 (agent, session) and 80 (tool-use) characters.

A8. docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-009: "Claude session IDs, input/output, tool events, native SDK failure and token usage are translated without invented values." and WB-025: "Workbench distinguishes Run/Work/Attempt, Forge operation and workspace basis, Claude session, HX coverage, RF provenance." -> with toolsTruncated true and 16 tools, exactly 16 tool-use snapshots exist, result.truncated is true and session coverage is 'partial'; no field named tokens, cost or usage exists on any snapshot; the whole suite runs with no TTY, no SDK, no network; two calls with identical input produce deep-equal, frozen output (Object.isFrozen on result, snapshots and relations) and JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(result)) deep-equals result.

title: W16-B/VC-4: pure bounded workflow_observe reply builder over ObservationProjection (cursor pagination, selectors, relation and event-window metadata, last-known-running + stale freshness summary, byte cap, sanitized compact JSON); Pi tool registration excluded
description:
Gap (measured at rig HEAD ad3cf6e908f0): the registered workflow_observe tool (src/index.ts:2593-2622, hot) returns projection.query({scope, invocationId, limit}) nodes plus truncated and task fields, and furnace_observe (src/index.ts:2549-2570, hot) returns the raw FurnaceReading; neither offers a cursor, selectors, relation or event-window metadata, a freshness summary or a response byte cap, while W16 (wb-69g) names "compact bounded result and ACL" as its acceptance. docs/workbench/11 proposes workflow_observe(ref, selectors?, cursor?, limit?) returning "bounded native snapshot, event window, aggregates, freshness, anomaly evidence"; docs/workbench/09 requires Pi tool summaries to communicate "last-known-running + stale"; docs/workbench/14 lists "Pi model tool response size under bounded queries" as a benchmark measure. ObservationProjection already exposes every read needed: window({scope, invocationId, offset, limit}) -> {nodes, total, revision} (src/workbench/observation.ts:448), relations({scope, from?, to?, limit?}) (:397), events({scope, limit, ref?, after?}) -> {events, truncated, completeness} (:540), relationRevision() (:467) and stats() (:558). The ACL (grants, session/workspace/principal checks) stays in the hot tool; this bead delivers the reply shaping the tool will later call.

Scope (atomic, additive, hot-file free): src/workbench/observe-query.ts (new) exporting
- OBSERVE_CONTRACT = "workbench.observe/v1"; type ObserveReader = Pick<ObservationProjection, "window" | "relations" | "events" | "relationRevision" | "stats">.
- interface ObserveRequest { scope: ObservationScope; invocationId: string; cursor?: string; limit?: number (1..40, default 20); selectors?: { tone?: Presentation["statusTone"]; kind?: string; relations?: boolean; events?: { limit: number (1..40) } }; maxBytes?: number (1024..65536, default 16384) }.
- observeInvocation(reader: ObserveReader, request: ObserveRequest): ObserveReply, pure and synchronous: calls only reader methods (window once per call; relations at most once per returned node with limit <= 40 when selectors.relations; events once when selectors.events); never ingest/refresh/relate/markStale, never a provider.

description:
Gap (measured at rig HEAD ad3cf6e908f0, branch workbench/implementation-program): docs/workbench/15 § "Implementation status at 2026-10-15" records VC-1 as experimental because "actual terminal operator and live adverse cancellation acceptance remain open", and the VC-1 cut requires "Ctrl-C/cancel and invalid model/permission failures behave explicitly." TRACEABILITY.md WB-010 ("Stopping the parent propagates cancellation only through established ownership and appropriate SDK API") is experimental with an empty live column. The code paths exist: src/workflow/runtime.ts RunWorkflowOptions.signal (line 323) finishes the run as { status: "killed", error: "Workflow aborted." } (line 867) after host.abortAgent(agentId) for every in-flight agent (line 853); src/workbench/claude-host.ts keeps one AbortController per agent (lines 98/156), passes it to the SDK query as abortController (line 171), aborts it in abortAgent (line 268) and returns { ok:false, skipped:true, error:"Claude SDK query was cancelled.", sessionId? } (lines 207/218/247), with onMessage/onSettled hooks (lines 42-43). Nothing exercises these against a real SDK session: qa/workbench/live-claude.mjs and live-resume.mjs prove only the happy path, test/workbench-host-contract.test.ts uses a fixture query, and forge.toml has no cancellation tier.

Scope (atomic, measurement-only, hot-file free; src/ untouched):
1. qa/workbench/live-adverse-receipt.mjs (new, pure, no src/ or dist/ import): assessAdverseJourneys(observed) -> { findings: {rule, detail}[], realised: boolean } and buildAdverseReceipt(input) -> frozen plain object { contract: "workbench.claude-adverse/v1", utc, revision, node, arch, platform, sdkVersion, model, journeys, sdkEventTypes, findings, realised, pass }. The builder throws if any string field matches /Bearer\s+\S+|sk-ant-|api[_-]?key/i or contains \x1b (redaction is the runner's job; the receipt must never carry a credential).
2. qa/workbench/live-adverse.mjs (new runner; imports ONLY ../../dist/workbench/claude-host.js, ../../dist/workflow/runtime.js, ../../dist/workbench/redaction.js and @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk getSessionInfo; cwd = argv[2] ?? process.cwd(); no vi.mock, no query override, no Pi AgentManager). One real host per journey: createClaudeWorkflowHost({cwd, model: process.env.CLAUDE_ADVERSE_MODEL ?? "claude-opus-5-5", tools: [], settingSources: [], permissionMode: "dontAsk", onMessage, onSettled}).
   J1 mid-stream cancel: the script runs parallel([agent(long prompt A), agent(long prompt B)]) where each prompt asks for about 600 words so the stream outlives the abort; an AbortController passed as the runWorkflow signal is aborted on the FIRST onMessage with type "system", subtype "init" and a session_id (fault location "after Claude SDK session ID first received"); record requestedAt. onSettled records per-agent acknowledgedAt and the host result. runWorkflow resolution records terminalAt and the outcome.
   J2 pre-start abort: the controller is aborted BEFORE runWorkflow is called; expect status "killed" and zero SDK messages.
   J3 invalid model: model "claude-adverse-not-a-model-000" (override CLAUDE_ADVERSE_INVALID_MODEL); expect a non-completed outcome with an explicit redacted error and no ok:true settled result.
3. Exit semantics (receipt printed as one JSON line and written to $CLAUDE_ADVERSE_RECEIPT when set, BEFORE exiting): 0 = realised and no findings; 1 = realised with findings (a measured violation, recorded honestly, never tuned away); 2 = not realised (gateway unreachable or unauthenticated, every J1 agent settled before the abort landed, or J3 accepted the model) with a diagnostic naming the unrealised journey. A missing or unauthenticated gateway is exit 2 with the redacted SDK error, never a skip and never a fixture substitute.
4. forge.toml: one additive [build.commands.claude-adverse-live] block (command "node qa/workbench/live-adverse.mjs", timeout 300), NOT added to the default [build] gate list (same placement as claude-live).
5. test/workbench-claude-adverse-receipt.test.ts (new vitest, offline, no network, no SDK): imports the assessor/builder from ../qa/workbench/live-adverse-receipt.mjs and runs the negative fixtures in the acceptance; also reads qa/workbench/live-adverse.mjs as text and asserts its import specifiers are exactly the allowed set above and that it contains no "vi.mock", no "query:" option and no "AgentManager".

Out of scope: editing src/workbench/claude-host.ts, src/workflow/runtime.ts or any src/ file (if J1 measures a violation, record the finding in the ledger line and the bead notes and return blocked; the fix is hot-set work); the Pi tool/TUI Ctrl-C operator journey (separate acceptance); resume-after-cancel; invalid permission-mode journeys; editing qa/workbench/live-claude.mjs; editing docs/TRACEABILITY.md.

Files: qa/workbench/live-adverse-receipt.mjs (new), qa/workbench/live-adverse.mjs (new), test/workbench-claude-adverse-receipt.test.ts (new), forge.toml (one additive block).
acceptance_criteria:
Red-first: test/workbench-claude-adverse-receipt.test.ts fails before qa/workbench/live-adverse-receipt.mjs exists. All quotes are from docs/workbench in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program).

J1. Cancellation is explicit, never a completion. After the abort on the first init message, outcome.status === "killed" and outcome.error === "Workflow aborted."; outcome.value is undefined; no agent in flight at requestedAt has a settled result with ok === true; every cancelled agent's settled result is { ok: false, skipped: true, error: "Claude SDK query was cancelled." } carrying the sessionId the SDK reported; agents the SDK finished BEFORE requestedAt are counted as settledBeforeCancel (reported, not a failure), and the journey is realised only if agentsCancelled >= 1, else exit 2. Quote docs/workbench/15-implementation-program.md § "Vertical cuts" VC-1: "Ctrl-C/cancel and invalid model/permission failures behave explicitly." Quote docs/workbench/04-claude-agent-sdk-executor.md § "Tests": "No false successful tool or domain verdict after SDK result error".

J2. Three phases with their own timestamps. The receipt records requestedAt (abort call), acknowledgedAt per cancelled agent (onSettled delivering the cancellation result) and terminalAt (runWorkflow resolved), with requestedAt <= each acknowledgedAt <= terminalAt; requestToAckMs and ackToTerminalMs are measured numbers; the receipt never reports a phase it did not observe (acknowledgedAt is absent for an agent whose onSettled never fired, and the assessor then records finding "unacknowledged-agent"). Quote docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "State/event semantics": "Cancellation request != accepted cancellation != terminal cancellation." Quote docs/workbench/04-claude-agent-sdk-executor.md § "Cancellation and steering": "Cancellation request != terminal acknowledgement."

J3. Cancellation is scoped to owned sessions and starts nothing new. After requestedAt no further SDK message of type "system"/subtype "init" is observed (initAfterAbort === 0); the number of distinct session_ids equals the number of agents started before requestedAt; every observed session_id matches /^[a-f0-9-]{36}$/ and getSessionInfo(sessionId, {dir: cwd}) returns a record whose sessionId equals it after the run (the native record exists and is neither invented nor deleted). Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-010: "Stopping the parent propagates cancellation only through established ownership and appropriate SDK API; stopping observation does not." Quote docs/workbench/04-claude-agent-sdk-executor.md § "Cancellation and steering": "Keep SDK AbortController (or supported SDK stop API) scoped to exactly one owned Claude invocation." Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-009: "Claude session IDs, input/output, tool events, native SDK failure and token usage are translated without invented values."

J4. Pre-start abort creates no native work. With the signal already aborted before runWorkflow, outcome.status === "killed", sdkMessages === 0 and sessionIds is empty. Quote docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Fault-injection locations": "Before/after Claude SDK session ID first received; during tool execution; after output tokens streamed but before final." Quote docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md § "Runtime and host requirements": "A Pi UI reconnect is only an observer/client action; it must not restart external work."

J5. Invalid model fails explicitly. With the invalid model, outcome.status !== "completed", outcome.error is a non-empty string passed through redactWorkbenchText (at most 400 characters, no control characters), no settled result has ok === true, and sessionIds carries only ids the SDK actually reported (possibly none); if the gateway accepts the model and completes, the journey is unrealised (exit 2, finding "invalid-model-accepted"), never a pass. Quote docs/workbench/04-claude-agent-sdk-executor.md § "Tests": "Negative: invalid model, absent credentials, malformed native output, stream error after partial text, aborted query, resumed unknown session, inaccessible cwd, invalid tool policy." Quote docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md § "Error and degradation policy": "Missing Claude auth -> clear config error; do not silently use Pi model."

J6. Real SDK or nothing. The runner imports only ../../dist/workbench/claude-host.js, ../../dist/workflow/runtime.js, ../../dist/workbench/redaction.js and @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk (the vitest guard asserts the import list from the file text and the absence of "vi.mock", "query:" and "AgentManager"); an unreachable or unauthenticated gateway yields exit 2 with the redacted SDK error in the receipt, never exit 0 and never a substitute. Quote docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Test classes" C: "Integration: real Claude Agent SDK in supported test environment, actual native SDK provider version and evidence; use fixture substitutes only in tests explicitly named fixture." Quote docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md § "Current experimental distribution": "Missing fixture settings fail rather than skip. Their receipts establish only the surfaces actually exercised."

J7. Evidence-grade, redacted receipt. The receipt carries contract "workbench.claude-adverse/v1", utc, revision (git rev-parse HEAD or the literal "working-tree"), node, arch, platform, sdkVersion read from node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/package.json (0.3.300 at HEAD, never hardcoded), model, journeys, sdkEventTypes, findings, realised and pass; it contains no assistant text, prompt text or tool payload (only ids, types, counts, timestamps and redacted error previews), and the pure builder throws on any value matching /Bearer\s+\S+|sk-ant-|api[_-]?key/i or containing \x1b. Quote docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Truth labels and release gates": "Every test evidence artifact includes revision, tool versions, commands, timestamp, host, native references and actual output." Quote docs/workbench/12-security.md § "Credential boundaries": "redact tokens from logs, UI, recordings and failure messages." Quote docs/workbench/04-claude-agent-sdk-executor.md § "Streaming and progress": "Avoid printing secrets or tool payloads in overview."

J8. Offline falsifiers in test/workbench-claude-adverse-receipt.test.ts (no network, no SDK import): an agent in flight at requestedAt that settles ok:true -> finding "completed-after-cancel"; an init message after requestedAt -> finding "init-after-abort"; agentsCancelled === 0 -> realised false; a pre-start journey with sdkMessages 1 -> finding "work-before-start"; an invalid-model journey with status "completed" -> finding "invalid-model-accepted"; a receipt input containing "Authorization: Bearer abc123" -> the builder throws; a clean fixture -> pass true with every J7 field present. title: W22-B: packed npm artifact boundary falsifier (top-level allowlist, agent-tooling denylist, bundled-only node_modules, .npmignore fix for tracked .agents/ and .codex/) plus evidence-grade package-smoke receipt (revision, toolchain, host, pack determinism)
description:
Gap (measured at rig HEAD ad3cf6e908f0, branch workbench/implementation-program): `npm pack --dry-run --ignore-scripts --json` packs 374 files including the git-tracked agent-tooling files `.agents/skills/beads/SKILL.md`, `.agents/skills/beads/agents/openai.yaml`, `.codex/config.toml` and `.codex/hooks.json`. `.codex/hooks.json` wires `bd codex-hook` commands to SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit/PreCompact/PostCompact, so a consumer who opens the installed package directory in Codex inherits hook commands from the npm artifact. `.npmignore` already excludes `.pi`, `.claude`, `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` under its own heading "Internal contributor/agent instructions — not for distribution" but omits `.agents/` and `.codex/`. qa/workbench/package-smoke.mjs (default forge gate step `package-smoke`) denies only the `.beads/` and `.forge/` prefixes, and its receipt `{contract:"workbench.package-smoke/v1", fileCount, sha, integrity, privateStateIncluded}` records no revision, tool versions, timestamp, host or command, contrary to the docs/workbench/14 truth-label rule. Packed `node_modules/` content is today exactly the three `inBundle: true` package-lock entries (@forge/sdk 49 files, @furnace/sdk 79, @hyperunix/sdk 111); nothing asserts that.

Scope (atomic, hot-file free, no src/ edits):
1. `.npmignore`: add `.agents/` and `.codex/` under the existing "Internal contributor/agent instructions" heading. Change nothing else (qa/, docs/, examples/ keep shipping as today; see notes).
2. `qa/workbench/package-boundary.mjs` (new, plain ESM, no dependencies): export TOP_LEVEL_ALLOWLIST (LICENSE, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, package.json, forge.toml, dist, src, docs, examples, qa, vendor, node_modules), DENIED_PREFIXES (.agents/, .codex/, .pi/, .claude/, .beads/, .forge/, .furnace/, .hyperunix/, .reactive-fiber/, .github/, machines/, test/, tests/), DENIED_BASENAMES (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, biome.json, tsconfig.json), DENIED_PATTERNS (basename matches /\.jsonl$/, /^vitest\..*config\.ts$/ or /\.test\.ts$/), `classifyPackedPaths(paths, { bundledLockEntries })` returning `{ violations: {path, rule}[], topLevel: string[] }` where a `node_modules/` path is a violation unless its (scope-aware) package name is in bundledLockEntries (the package-lock `packages` entry names whose `inBundle === true`), and a pure `buildPackageReceipt(input)` that assembles the v2 receipt from already-measured values.
3. `qa/workbench/package-smoke.mjs`: keep every existing v1 assertion verbatim; add classifyPackedPaths over the pack listing (any violation fails the smoke listing every offending path and rule); pack the same tree a second time and assert identical `shasum` and `integrity`; emit receipt `contract: "workbench.package-smoke/v2"` with the v1 fields plus revision (`git rev-parse HEAD`, or the literal `unknown:not-a-git-checkout`), dirty (true/false from `git status --porcelain`, or null when revision is unknown), node (process.version), npm (`npm --version`), platform, arch, utc, command, topLevel (sorted), bundled (sorted lock entry names), denied (always [] on success).
4. `test/workbench-package-boundary.test.ts` (new vitest; no npm child process, no network): imports the classifier and receipt builder from `../qa/workbench/package-boundary.mjs`, runs the fixture cases in acceptance item 6, unit-tests the receipt builder with fake git results, and parses `.npmignore` asserting the required exclusion lines.

Out of scope (flag in the ledger line, do not change): whether `qa/` development runners and `docs/` should ship; a package.json `exports` map; version bump; npm publication; editing docs/TRACEABILITY.md or docs/workbench/*; forge.toml. If any step needs a hot file or a src/ change, stop and return blocked.

Files: .npmignore; qa/workbench/package-smoke.mjs; qa/workbench/package-boundary.mjs (new); test/workbench-package-boundary.test.ts (new).
acceptance_criteria:
All criteria quote docs/workbench specs in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program) or the rig's own .npmignore.

1. docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md § "Current experimental distribution": "The package contains a validated dependency-lock copy under `vendor/`, while producer-local Beads/Forge/Furnace/HX/RF stores are excluded." and .npmignore heading "Internal contributor/agent instructions — not for distribution" -> after the change `npm pack --dry-run --ignore-scripts --json` lists no path under `.agents/` or `.codex/`; package-smoke's denylist assertion is red on the pre-fix tree (printing the four offending paths) and green after the .npmignore edit; both command outputs are recorded in the ledger line.
2. docs/workbench/12-security.md § "Supply chain": "Avoid unrestricted dynamic plugin loading from arbitrary paths; provider packages require an allowlisted manifest/version/digest." and docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Truth labels and release gates": "Pin dependencies, lockfile and package exports." -> every packed `node_modules/` path belongs to a package whose package-lock entry has `inBundle: true` (today exactly @forge/sdk, @furnace/sdk, @hyperunix/sdk, derived from the lock at run time, not hardcoded); any other node_modules path and any top-level segment outside TOP_LEVEL_ALLOWLIST is a violation that fails the smoke with the offending paths and rule names printed.
3. docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Truth labels and release gates": "Every test evidence artifact includes revision, tool versions, commands, timestamp, host, native references and actual output." -> the receipt (`contract: "workbench.package-smoke/v2"`) carries revision, dirty, node, npm, platform, arch, utc, command, fileCount, shasum, integrity, topLevel, bundled, denied; when the tree is not a git checkout, revision is the literal `unknown:not-a-git-checkout` and dirty is null (never an invented SHA); buildPackageReceipt is pure and unit-tested with a fake git result for both the known and unknown cases.

title: W13/VC-2: Forge gate-status reader adapter projects NativeSnapshots and grouping edges (historical last_result stays unknown/partial, failed gate stays failed); tool wiring excluded
description:
Gap: the only NativeSnapshot producer in src/ is FurnaceObserver.projectionSnapshot (src/workbench/furnace-observer.ts, extended by wb-752.1); grep -rn "NativeSnapshot\|projectionSnapshot" src returns only that file and its hot consumer src/index.ts:2560. The real native Forge read (src/workbench/providers/forge.ts, invoke() result {contract:'forge.gate.status/v1', protocolMethod:'gate.status', source}) never reaches the ObservationProjection or the inspector. docs/workbench/09 § Reader adapters requires a read-current-snapshot function per supported provider, and docs/workbench/15 gates the P1 inspector release on "real native source". The measured native read of this workspace returned status=success with authoritative_current=false, which must appear as historical/indeterminate, never as a verified PASS.

Scope (atomic, additive, new file, hot-file free): src/workbench/forge-observer.ts exporting
- forgeGateTopology(reading: JsonValue, context: { scope: ObservationScope; target: string; capturedAt: string; observedAt: string; invocationId?: string }): { snapshots: NativeSnapshot[]; relations: ForgeObservedRelation[]; diagnostics: string[] } where ForgeObservedRelation is exactly the parameter type of ObservationProjection.relate.
- Validation: reading must be the exact provider output (contract 'forge.gate.status/v1', protocolMethod 'gate.status', source.envelope.reason_code string, source.data.packages an array of objects with a string ref of at most 256 bytes and no control characters); anything else throws CapabilityError('validation'). Unknown extra producer fields are tolerated, never required and never copied into presentation text.
- One workspace snapshot: source {provider:'forge', type:'gate-status', id:'workspace', scope: context.target}, kind 'forge.gate.status.snapshot', node.type 'sdk-operation', statusText built from source.status, envelope.verdict and envelope.reason_code (e.g. "partial · COULD_NOT_JUDGE · FORGE_GATE_INCOMPLETE · verification indeterminate"), statusTone 'unknown' unless every package is authoritative_current === true (then 'failure' if any last_result === 'failure', 'success' only if all last_result === 'success'), coverage 'partial' when source.status !== 'success' or any package is not authoritative_current, otherwise 'complete'; sourceVersion 'forge.gate.status/v1'; evidenceRefs ['forge:gate.status:<reason_code>'].
- One snapshot per package: source {provider:'forge', type:'gate-status', id: pkg.ref, scope: context.target}, statusText "<last_result> (historical; authoritative_current=false[; <unverified_reason>])" with statusTone 'unknown' whenever authoritative_current !== true; when authoritative_current === true, statusText "<last_result> (current)" with statusTone 'success' for last_result 'success', 'failure' for 'failure', 'unknown' otherwise. Never an interval (Forge gate status carries no timestamps), never subjectBasis (a target path is not a basis), never definitionDigest.
- One 'grouping' relation workspace->package per package with provenance {source:'forge-observer', observedAt: context.observedAt}; never 'ownership' (the gate.status envelope carries no native lifecycle confirmation reference, and relate() rejects ownership without one) and never 'dependency'/'causation'/'hypothesis'.
- All presentation text passes redactWorkbenchText (import from src/workbench/redaction.ts, hot — do not edit) and is bounded to 200 characters so ObservationProjection.refresh never throws on producer text.

Out of scope: registering or wiring the adapter into furnace_observe/workflow_observe (src/index.ts, hot), providers/forge.ts changes (the adapter consumes its output), inspector text assertions or changes (wb-6ze.1 owns src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts this round), any Forge write or gate.run.
Files: src/workbench/forge-observer.ts (new); test/workbench-forge-observer.test.ts (new). Fixture: reuse the SOURCE shape from test/workbench-forge-contract.test.ts.
acceptance_criteria:
Red-first: test/workbench-forge-observer.test.ts fails before src/workbench/forge-observer.ts exists. Quotes are from docs/workbench in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program).

F1 Historical result is not a verdict. With SOURCE = {status:'success', envelope:{verdict:null, reason_code:'FORGE_OK'}, data:{packages:[{ref:'code:pi-subagents', last_result:'success', authoritative_current:false, unverified_reason:'FORGE_CURRENT_STATE_UNVERIFIED'}]}} wrapped as {contract:'forge.gate.status/v1', protocolMethod:'gate.status', source: SOURCE}: exactly two snapshots; the package snapshot has statusTone 'unknown', statusText containing 'historical', 'authoritative_current=false' and 'FORGE_CURRENT_STATE_UNVERIFIED', coverage 'partial'; JSON.stringify(result) does not contain '"statusTone":"success"'. Quote docs/workbench/00-current-state-and-source-map.md § "2026-10-15 implementation update (experimental; evidence-scoped)": "authoritative_current=false (historical status, not current verification). That latter field is preserved without a fabricated PASS." Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-015: "Workbench cannot turn absent/unknown/partial producer evidence into successful domain verdict."

F2 Failed gate stays failed; current success is success. authoritative_current true with last_result 'failure' -> package statusTone 'failure' and workspace statusTone 'failure' even though source.status is 'success'; authoritative_current true with last_result 'success' -> 'success' and coverage 'complete'. Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Acceptance/negative controls" item 7: "A true Forge failed gate remains failed despite transport success." Quote docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Matrix by subsystem" Forge row: "gate on exact candidate/basis with producer verdict | source basis changed -> no PASS".

F3 Partial envelope is indeterminate, not empty success. {status:'partial', envelope:{verdict:'COULD_NOT_JUDGE', reason_code:'FORGE_GATE_INCOMPLETE'}, data:{packages:[]}} -> one workspace snapshot with statusTone 'unknown', statusText containing 'COULD_NOT_JUDGE' and 'indeterminate', coverage 'partial', zero package snapshots, zero relations, and one diagnostic naming the empty package list. Quote docs/workbench/19-worked-examples.md § "Example H: native evidence refusal": "Pi must show \"verification indeterminate\", not success, even if host RPC returned normally and text says \"build completed\"."

F4 Contract validation fails closed. contract 'hyperunix.find/v1', protocolMethod 'gate.run', missing envelope.reason_code, packages not an array, a package without a string ref, or a ref longer than 256 bytes each throw CapabilityError with category 'validation'; an extra unknown field on a package or the envelope is tolerated and never appears in any statusText. Quote docs/workbench/13-contracts-and-config.md § "Key validations": "unrecognized SDK message version => diagnostic rather than silent success." Quote docs/workbench/06-capability-registry.md § "Registration and resolution": "validate output representation without erasing unknown producer fields."

F5 Only grouping edges, no invented lifecycle or timing. Every relation has kind 'grouping' and provenance.source 'forge-observer'; relations.length === packages.length; no snapshot carries interval, subjectBasis or definitionDigest. Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Relationships are typed and provenanced": "lifecycle ownership (only if native producer confirms)" and "grouping only (phase, display scope)". Quote docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md § "Four views" Timeline: "Never infer exact timing from text or assume clocks agree; note uncertain clocks or event gaps." Quote test/workbench-native-evidence.test.ts case title: "preserves Forge native operation and partial status but never workspace path as basis".

F6 Read-model integration. Applying snapshots via ObservationProjection.refresh and relations via relate on a real projection: query({scope, parent: workspaceRef, limit: 10}) returns exactly the package nodes; query({scope, statusTone:'unknown', limit: 10}) includes the historical package; every relations({scope, from: workspaceKey}) entry is 'grouping'; a second forgeGateTopology call with the same reading and a later observedAt refreshes without duplicating nodes (stats().nodes unchanged). Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Reader adapters": "Reader adapter returns snapshot {nativeRef, capturedAt, observedAt, sourceRevision?, coverage?, nativePayloadRef}". Quote docs/workbench/15-implementation-program.md § "Gating policy": "P1 inspector release requires VC-4/VC-5 with real native source and scale benchmark."

F7 Bounded, redacted presentation. A reason_code of 10,000 characters containing 'Bearer abc123' and '\x1b[31m' yields statusText of at most 200 characters with no control characters, containing '[REDACTED]' and not 'abc123', and refresh() does not throw. Quote docs/workbench/12-security.md § "Input and output hardening": "Validate Unicode and terminal escape sequences before display (no untrusted ANSI injection)." Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Acceptance/negative controls" item 10: "Large/secret payload does not leak into Pi tool result or screen by default."

F8 Native status is not replaced by tone. statusText always contains the literal native last_result / verdict strings; the test asserts that native 'success' and tone 'unknown' coexist in the F1 package snapshot. Quote docs/workbench/13-contracts-and-config.md § "Observation projection": "Do not replace native status with presentation.statusTone. This is a read model only."

F9 Gate: ./node_modules/.bin/biome check --write on touched files; npm run typecheck clean (no any, no inline imports); ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run test/workbench-forge-observer.test.ts test/workbench-forge-contract.test.ts test/workbench-native-evidence.test.ts test/workbench-observation.test.ts green; existing tests untouched; record red and green commands in the delivered ledger line; do not edit docs/TRACEABILITY.md (acceptance owner reconciles).

Preserve authoritative_current semantics: historical green never presented as current verification; transport success never PASS; outputs route through shared sanitizers (src/workbench/redaction.ts). title: W14/VC-5: Incremental ancestor aggregates over observed grouping/ownership edges in ObservationProjection (measured counts, interval envelope, incomplete-trace label; inspector wiring excluded)
description:
Gap: ObservationProjection (src/workbench/observation.ts) keeps flat per-node indexes (status, kind, basis, evidence, version, time) but no ancestor aggregate: nothing answers "how many observed children/descendants does this group or Run have, in which status tones, with which interval envelope" without re-walking relations per frame. docs/workbench/10 requires ancestor aggregates to be maintained incrementally and the overview to show "status and counts"; docs/workbench/09 § Aggregates and profiling requires measured counts with an explicit "incomplete trace" label instead of a precise critical path. wb-9x5.2 (W21-A, seat g1) explicitly deferred "adding ancestor/supernode aggregation to observation.ts or workflow-inspector.ts" to a follow-up; wb-6ze.1 (W15 nested tree) is confined to the inspector and uses no new projection API. This bead supplies the read-model half only.

Scope (atomic, additive, hot-file free), all inside src/workbench/observation.ts:
- export interface AncestorAggregate { key: string; revision: number; topologyRevision: number; direct: { children: number; settled: number; byTone: Record<Presentation["statusTone"], number> }; descendants: { counted: number; byTone: Record<Presentation["statusTone"], number>; stale: number; depthReached: number; truncated: boolean }; intervals: { known: number; missing: number; open: number; earliestStartedAt?: string; latestEndedAt?: string }; trace: "incomplete" | "bounded"; criticalPath: "unestablished"; basis: "observed-grouping-ownership" }
- aggregate(filter: { scope: ObservationScope; key: string }): AncestorAggregate | undefined — a copied value; undefined for unknown or cross-scope keys without any traversal.
- aggregateStats(): { adjustments: number; rebuilds: number; maxVisitedPerUpdate: number } (additive; the existing stats() shape {nodes, events, edges} is unchanged).
Child edges are outgoing relations of kind 'grouping' or 'ownership' (parent = from, child = to). Set semantics: a descendant is counted once per ancestor even through diamonds. Depth cap AGGREGATE_DEPTH = 8 (same cap as wb-6ze.1); cycles terminate at the first repeated key. 'dependency', 'causation' and 'hypothesis' edges never trigger or contribute. Hot path: a node's status/interval/freshness change (ingest, refresh, markStale, disconnect, reconnect) adjusts its ancestors by walking incoming grouping/ownership edges with a per-walk visited set — O(depth x fan-in), never a scan of nodes or events. Topology changes (relate/removeEdge of grouping/ownership edges, discard/eviction) rebuild only the affected ancestors from their bounded subtree. settled = success + failure tones; stale = descendants whose freshness !== 'current'; intervals use source intervals only (earliest startedAt, latest endedAt; an open interval increments open and never fabricates an end); trace is 'incomplete' whenever intervals.missing > 0 or descendants.truncated; criticalPath is the literal 'unestablished' (no number, no estimate, no token or cost fields).

Out of scope: rendering counts in src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts (reserved this round by wb-6ze.1 and wb-g1g.1; a later bead wires overview counts), workflow_observe tool output (src/index.ts, hot), supernode collapse, concurrency/critical-path profiling, any cap change.
Files: src/workbench/observation.ts (edit, additive); test/workbench-observation-aggregates.test.ts (new). test/workbench-observation*.test.ts, test/workbench-projection-invalidation.test.ts and test/workbench-inspector*.test.ts stay verbatim and green.
acceptance_criteria:
Red-first: test/workbench-observation-aggregates.test.ts fails before aggregate()/aggregateStats() exist. All quotes are from docs/workbench in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program).

A1 Brute-force equality (falsifier). A seeded deterministic fixture (no Date.now()/Math.random() in the measured path, same rules as the header of test/helpers/perf-fixtures.ts) builds >= 500 nodes with grouping and ownership edges up to depth 8 including diamonds, plus dependency/causation/hypothesis edges; after every batch of status/interval/freshness mutations and edge additions, aggregate(key) for every key deep-equals an independent brute-force recomputation over grouping/ownership reachability with set semantics. Quote docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md § "Rendering pipeline": "Avoid O(allHistory) collapse per frame; maintain by-node last projection and ancestor aggregates incrementally." Quote docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Truth labels and release gates": "Each major work package must have a falsifier: a negative test that would fail if a critical guarantee was quietly weakened."

A2 Only observed hierarchy counts. A dependency/causation/hypothesis-only fixture yields direct.children === 0 and descendants.counted === 0 for every key; adding a 'grouping' edge changes the parent's aggregate, adding a 'hypothesis' edge between the same pair does not. Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Relationships are typed and provenanced": "lifecycle ownership (only if native producer confirms)", "grouping only (phase, display scope)", "inferred possible relationship (hypothesis; never treated as authoritative)". Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-037: "Source-defined edges, observed edges and inferred links are distinguishable."

A3 Incremental propagation and depth cap. On a 10-level grouping chain, flipping the leaf from active to success increments descendants.byTone.success and settled at each ancestor within 8 levels, leaves the 9th and 10th ancestors unchanged with descendants.truncated === true and depthReached === 8, and aggregateStats().maxVisitedPerUpdate <= 8 for that flip. Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-029: "Over 1000 nodes: render cost scales with visible slice and changed ancestors; no full historical-log fold per frame."

A4 Cycles and diamonds terminate. Grouping cycle A->B->A: both aggregates are finite (descendants.counted === 1 each), the test completes, depthReached <= 8; a diamond P->X, P->Y, X->Z, Y->Z counts Z once in aggregate(P) (descendants.counted === 3). Quote docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md § "Four views" Graph: "Cycles/unknown dynamic edges represented explicitly as \"references\" rather than rendered as a fake acyclic plan."

A5 Eviction and edge removal subtract. With maxNodes/maxEdges limits forcing FIFO eviction, discarding a counted child or evicting its grouping edge brings the ancestors' counts back to the brute-force value; stats() keeps the existing {nodes, events, edges} shape so test/workbench-observation-perf.test.ts toEqual stays green. Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Derived view indexes": "Coalesce same-node repeated updates; do not rebuild entire history on each render."

A6 Measured intervals, no fabricated timing. Descendants with intervals give earliestStartedAt/latestEndedAt equal to the min startedAt / max endedAt of source intervals; a descendant with an open interval increments intervals.open and leaves latestEndedAt undefined; a descendant without an interval increments intervals.missing and sets trace 'incomplete'; criticalPath === 'unestablished' always, and JSON.stringify(aggregate) contains no numeric critical-path, token, cost or estimated field. Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Aggregates and profiling": "Distinguish measured actual from estimated projected metrics. If dependencies or interval bounds are missing, suppress precise critical path claims and show \"incomplete trace\". Derive latency decomposition only with valid source intervals." Quote docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md § "Four views" Overview: "Critical path must be shown as *partial/estimated* when relationships/times incomplete."

A7 Freshness rollup. disconnect('furnace') raises descendants.stale to the number of non-current descendants; reconnect alone leaves it unchanged; a refresh() snapshot lowers it. Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Freshness and ambiguity": "A disconnected Furnace event stream must not make a previously RUNNING node permanently authoritative RUNNING; it becomes last-known-running + stale." and "UI shows STALE/UNKNOWN visibly."

A8 Bounded work at scale. A 2,000-node, 5-level grouped tree receiving 100,000 status ingests: aggregateStats().maxVisitedPerUpdate <= 8 and aggregateStats().rebuilds does not grow with status updates (rebuilds count only topology changes); the median per-ingest time at 200 nodes vs 2,000 nodes is printed in the test output (reported, not asserted beyond the visit bound). Quote docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md § "Rendering pipeline": "For large graphs show aggregate supernodes first." Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-045: "Hierarchical agent-swarm aggregation and profile comparisons handle 10k+ nodes subject to benchmarked limits."

A9 Scope isolation. aggregate() with a key from another workspace/principal returns undefined and leaves aggregateStats() unchanged. Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Data retention and privacy": "Tenant/workspace boundaries apply at correlation queries, not just at individual SDK calls."

A10 Gate: ./node_modules/.bin/biome check --write on touched files; npm run typecheck clean (no any, no inline imports); ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run test/workbench-observation.test.ts test/workbench-observation-perf.test.ts test/workbench-projection-invalidation.test.ts test/workbench-inspector.test.ts test/workbench-inspector-window.test.ts test/workbench-observation-aggregates.test.ts green; node qa/workbench/inspector-bench.mjs still exits 0 after npm run build; record red and green commands in the delivered ledger line; do not edit docs/TRACEABILITY.md (acceptance owner reconciles).
notes: Sr. Engineer constraint 2026-10-15: observation.ts changes keep every existing invariant green (scoped markStale, out-of-order refusal, revision semantics, cross-scope isolation, 100k/1000 benchmark) and stay bounded. Aggregates derive from observed edges only — never fabricate ownership. Base on ad3cf6e+.
close_reason: Landed on workbench/implementation-program as merge a67bc36 (machine branch dee5a43, base 9c1c42f): incremental ancestor aggregates over observed grouping/ownership edges in src/workbench/observation.ts (AGGREGATE_DEPTH 8, AncestorAggregate, aggregate/aggregateStats) with test/workbench-observation-aggregates.test.ts (brute-force falsifier, eviction, scope isolation, FurnaceObserver roll-up). Relay gate cmd_3b47cb2d8b4b PASS; Sr. Engineer independent isolated-worktree complete gate on the merge PASS cmd_5eb54b7fe4fb (lint, typing, build, test, workbench-shell, package-smoke). Surface verified as exactly the two files, observation.ts unchanged on trunk since base, no any, top-level imports, no replayedCount/WorkflowRunResult constructions.

title: W16-A: pure workflow_control decision module (grant+confirmed-ownership preconditions, observer-only and guessed-action refusal, requested/acknowledged/result receipt); Pi tool registration excluded
description:
Every `workflow_*` Pi tool and every `workbench:*` grant check lives in src/index.ts (hot, Sr. Engineer-owned), and native Furnace control would live in src/workbench/providers/furnace.ts (hot). W16's acceptance "compact bounded result and ACL" still needs a testable control core. Deliver it as ONE new source file and ONE new test file; register nothing.

src/workbench/control.ts (new), pure and provider-free:
- `interface NativeControlRequest { scope: ObservationScope; principal: { id: string; role?: string }; grants: readonly string[] | undefined; target: NativeRef; action: string; params?: JsonValue; invocationId: string; requestedAt: string }` (names follow docs/workbench/13 Host boundary `requestControl(req: NativeControlRequest): Promise<NativeControlReceipt>`; this bead implements the decision, not the host method).
- `decideControl(request, deps: { projection: ObservationProjection; now: () => string })` returns `{ decision: 'denied'; category: CapabilityErrorCategory; reason: string }` or `{ decision: 'permitted'; receipt: NativeControlReceipt }`.
- `NativeControlReceipt` phases are distinct and ordered: `requested` -> `acknowledged` -> `result`. Fields: contractVersion 'workbench.control/v1', requestId, principal, grant, policy (rule name), target, action, invocationId, ownershipConfirmationRef, requestedAt; `acknowledge(receipt, { acknowledgedAt, nativeAckRef })` and `settle(receipt, { outcome: 'completed'|'failed'|'cancelled'|'unknown'; nativeResultRef: string; settledAt })` return new frozen receipts and throw CapabilityError('validation') on out-of-order transitions or missing native references. The module never calls a provider, never mutates the projection, never fabricates acknowledged/result.
- Deny rules (first match wins, every rule has a test): grants undefined/non-array/non-string entries or any wildcard (`control:*`) -> authorization "unknown permission data"; grants containing only discover:/inspect:/observe: prefixes -> authorization "observer-only" regardless of action spelling (stop, STOP, terminate, __proto__); action not in the frozen per-provider allowlist (furnace: stop; claude-agent-sdk: interrupt; forge: cancel) -> validation "unknown action"; missing exact grant `control:<provider>.<action>` -> authorization; target key not in the request scope (different workspace/principal) -> authorization "cross-scope"; target lacking a projection `ownership` relation whose provenance.source === target.provider AND provenance.nativeConfirmationRef is a non-empty string (re-check both; do not trust the relation kind alone) -> authorization "no confirmed lifecycle ownership" (causation/grouping/hypothesis edges never qualify); destructive actions (stop, cancel, interrupt, kill, delete) without `params.confirmed === true` -> validation "operator confirmation required".
test/workbench-control.test.ts (new): one test per rule plus the phase-ordering falsifiers; no TTY, no providers, no network.
Out of scope: any edit to src/index.ts, src/workbench/providers/furnace.ts, src/workbench/claude-host.ts or other hot files; Pi tool registration; executing a native stop. If the worker finds registration necessary to satisfy acceptance, stop and return blocked.
acceptance_criteria:
All criteria quote docs/workbench specs in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program).
1. docs/workbench/11-designer-and-operator.md § "First public Pi tools (proposed)": "workflow_control(ref,action,params?): explicit native action after permission/preconditions; returns requested/acknowledged/result distinct." -> three distinct phase literals; `settle` on a `requested` receipt throws; `acknowledge` twice throws; a receipt can never carry phase `result` without a non-empty nativeResultRef.
2. docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "State/event semantics": "Cancellation request != accepted cancellation != terminal cancellation." -> JSON.stringify of a `requested` receipt contains neither "acknowledged" nor "completed"; the three receipts differ in phase and carry their own timestamps.
3. docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "Cancellation and ownership": "Multi-reader shared child MUST NOT be stopped merely because one reader closed Pi or stopped waiting. Child cancellation depends on explicit native owner rights and native API semantics." -> a target with only causation/grouping/hypothesis relations is denied; an `ownership` relation with provenance.source === target.provider and a non-empty nativeConfirmationRef permits; the receipt copies that nativeConfirmationRef as ownershipConfirmationRef.

title: W15-A: lazy bounded native evidence loader contract for inspector details (loaded on focus; unavailable is visible, never fabricated); dialog/host wiring excluded
description:

   - `interface EvidenceLoader { readonly provider: string; canLoad(ref: string): boolean; load(ref: string, context: { scope: ObservationScope; signal: AbortSignal; maxBytes: number }): Promise<EvidenceContent> }`.
   - `type EvidenceEntry = {state:'not-requested'} | {state:'loading'} | {state:'loaded'; provider: string; capturedAt: string; bytes: number; truncated: boolean; preview: readonly string[]} | {state:'unavailable'; reason:'no-loader'|'unauthorized'|'transport'|'timeout'|'too-large'}`.
   - `class EvidenceStore` constructed with `{ loaders: readonly EvidenceLoader[]; maxEntries: number; maxBytes: number; timeoutMs: number }`: `get(scope, ref): EvidenceEntry`, `request(scope, ref): Promise<void>` (idempotent while loading), `abort(scope, ref)`, LRU eviction keyed by JSON.stringify([workspace, principal, ref]); previews are produced by passing loader text through `redactWorkbenchText` (import from src/workbench/redaction.ts — do not edit) then `safeWorkflowTerminalText` (import from src/ui/workflow-card.ts — do not edit), split into bounded lines; raw payloads are never retained. When `model.evidence` is absent, today's rendering is unchanged (all existing inspector tests stay green).
3. Tests: test/workbench-evidence-loader.test.ts (new) and appended cases in test/workbench-inspector.test.ts (keep every existing case verbatim).

N collapsed (observed grouping)', mark rows with no observed parent explicitly, and make the graph view's fan-out line carry a real bounded count with '(partial)' when the relation page is full. R1 - N2 IS THE SINGLE EXCEPTION
N2 (owner ruling 2026-10-17T23:33Z) is THE single exception to the P6 literal "at most one window() call per rendered pane". The case is a stored row index at or past the end of a non-empty viewport, a page or more down, with no selection that resolves (index >= total > 0 and index >= page height). b5af586 said "Two cases keep a second read, both pinned". That sentence is withdrawn:

- "Both pinned" was false at c164d87: MX1 and MX2 survived (gate row 522 U1).

A row index the reducers never store adds no second read of its own:
- A fraction is read exactly as its whole part is.
- An index of 2^53 or more, or +Infinity, reads from the top. It takes a second read only past the end of a viewport longer than a page, which is N2's case.
- NaN, and a fraction whose centred page would start between rows, throw in the projection, as the two-read renderer (trunk blob 841c988) did. The refusal is "Invalid observation viewport offset or limit (1..100).".

title: wb-hqa retention key-reuse remedy (R479): onInit forgets the key's remembered terminal so a retried/resumed call's acknowledged interrupt settles its own terminal instead of refusing foreign/stale-observation
description:
Owner follow-up from the wb-hqa Cut 1 adversarial review (verifiers F1/F6, fixer disposition, rechecker residual
note): the retention key `${task.id}:${call.index}` is reused across attempts/turns of one call (retry via
src/ui/workflow-menu.ts task.control.retry(index) with the same index/agentId minted in src/workflow/runtime.ts;
resume via src/workbench/claude-host.ts resumeAgent -> onSettled(result, previous.call)). A terminal remembered from
an earlier attempt makes retain() in src/workbench/claude-control-observer.ts short-circuit and refuse the later
attempt's acknowledged interrupt (retry -> foreign-observation, resume -> stale-observation) within the 15-minute
TTL, so the later attempt's own terminal settles nothing and no result phase is minted. Hermetic repros of record:
/tmp/hqa-fix-keyreuse-retry.log, /tmp/hqa-fix-keyreuse-resume.log (re-reproduced by the rechecker on a fresh build).

RULED REMEDY (R479, this bead implements it): forget the key's remembered terminal when onInit fires for the key — a
new system/init on the key is a new query. Compatibility verified at review time: U6
(test/workbench-claude-control-observer.test.ts) and B10 (test/workbench-pi-claude-control.test.ts) have no init
between the remembered terminal and the retain, so both ruled rows stand unchanged. The alternative (gate the
short-circuit on sessionId AND observedAt >= acknowledgedAt, else park pending) is REJECTED: it changes B10's ruled
one-line stale-observation row.
