title: index.ts has no forge observation surface: the session projection never admits forge-operation nodes, so the booted workflow_control refuses every forge target as not-admitted even with the connection retained; ingest from the server's own started/terminal frames at retention (6hb.5 pre-window gap)
description:
FILED at the 6hb.5 pre-window measurement (owner, 2026-10-17): the booted extension's ObservationProjection never admits forge-operation nodes - src/index.ts has no forge observation surface (no caller of forgeGateTopology ingests into the session projection; grep: zero forge refresh/relate sites), so the registered workflow_control tool's decision core refuses every forge target as not-admitted even when the connection IS retained (wb-cra.1, landed executor path reachable only through a harness-owned projection). The wb-6hb.5 live journey therefore runs through createWorkflowControlTool with the production executor factory and a projection fed exclusively from the server's own operation.started frames, and records this gap as a named unrealised scenario.

title: HXFS-PI-R1: a push-authority seat lands Pi's HyperUnix feedback entry on origin/main, verified from outside
description:
## Statement
A Pi seat holding push authority shall land Pi's HyperUnix feedback entry (commit `c52116840a`, path `new-feedback/2026-10-15-pi-workbench-sdk-find-preserves-incomplete-coverage-and-refuses-absence/`) on HyperUnix-CLI `origin/main` per that repo's producer contract (one finding per commit staged by path, `docs(new-feedback): <claim> (hu)` header with the six uppercase body sections, no model/vendor names, pushed `HEAD:main` by fetch-rebase-retry and never force), and shall verify the landing with `git merge-base --is-ancestor <landed-sha> origin/main` from outside the pushing clone. The re-delivered commit SHOULD additionally carry the retained probe `hx-coverage-probe.mjs` (and its stdout capture) beside README.md as artifacts cited by file name in an appended `SELF-REVISION` paragraph, without altering the entry's findings, grades, names or SHAs; if the writer declines, the commit body says so. A side-branch commit is not a delivery and is invisible to HXFS's main-only feedback census.

## Rationale
CONFIRMED (both refuter lenses regrade CONFIRMED). HX's producer contract defines delivery as landing on main: "The delivery is the push. A file on your disk is not feedback; a file the maintainers can read on `origin/main` is." (HyperUnix-CLI:new-feedback/README.md:115-116@d60f277a26) and "Verify the sha you pushed from outside; a push receipt is not a landing." (:143-144). HXFS cut 0 censuses new-feedback/ on main (01-feedback-evidence.md:7; 11-feedback-governance.md:5,:48) and values positive controls of exactly Pi's kind (11:34). Measured: `c52116840a` is not an ancestor of origin/main (rc=1 at d60f277a26, at 4baec37fdd, and at bcc23e3e02 on 2026-10-17); it exists only on `origin/feedback/pi-workbench-20261015-delivery`; origin/main is not an ancestor of it, so fast-forward of the commit itself is impossible and the rebase path (:139) yields a new sha. The first triage graded the duty COVERED via wb-kqx; HXFS is the HyperUnix program whose census this non-landing defeats (the HX half of RELEASE-CLAIMS-AUDIT.md:283's deferred five-row boundary). Probe sub-clause contested and resolved: the refuter's host fact is refuted (ls 2026-10-17 shows hx-coverage-probe.mjs, 765 bytes, plus hx-coverage.json at /var/tmp/pi-feedback-delivery-20261015/); the policy half is accepted, hence SHOULD and additive, never a rewrite (wb-jwc.2 twin rule). Priority: seat bd 2 — CONFIRMED delivery duty, not a runtime mechanism; same class as rf twin wb-jwc.1.

## Acceptance criteria
1. From a fresh HyperUnix-CLI clone or a detached worktree based on origin/main (never the shared owner checkout — README.md:118-120): `git show --stat --name-only <sha>` lists only paths under the entry directory. RED today: c52116840a lists 1 file (README.md) and its :23 cites a host path `/var/tmp/pi-feedback-delivery-20261015/hx-coverage-probe.mjs` against README.md:41-43 ("A finding cites its artifacts by file name.").
2. If the SHOULD is taken: the directory also holds `hx-coverage-probe.mjs` (byte-identical to the retained copy, 765 bytes) and `hx-coverage.json` (its stdout, 133,553 bytes), README.md gains one appended `SELF-REVISION` paragraph citing both by file name, and the README diff vs c52116840a shows additions only. If not taken: the commit body contains the sentence that the probe was not committed.
3. `git log -1 --format=%s <sha>` matches the `docs(new-feedback): <claim> (hu)` subject shape; the body contains each of PROBLEM, ROOT CAUSE, SOLUTION, TDD TESTING, RISKS AND URGENCY, PROVENANCE (README.md:123-126); the vendor-name grep over the commit prints nothing (README.md:126-127).
4. `sh tools/lint/feedback-layout.sh <sha>` exits 0 (README.md:14-15).
5. Before pushing, the writer re-reads `ls new-feedback/ | grep -i -- coverage` and `docs/feedback-dispositions.jsonl` (README.md:47-50,:148-153) and decides whether the on-main entry beginning `2026-10-16-run24-12-dogfood-hx-hx-find-states-one-fs-coverage-gap-as-completeness-incomplete-...` is the same mechanism; if yes, the directory is re-stamped `CORROBORATION-` with `**Corroborates:** <entry> — verdict STILL-TRUE` (prefix convention README.md:38-40; the `**Corroborates:**` format literal is README.md:80); either decision is recorded in the commit body.
6. Push is `git push origin HEAD:main` after `git fetch` + `git rebase origin/main` (README.md:139); no force flag appears in the shell transcript. Then, from a clone other than the pushing one: `git fetch -q origin && git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/main; echo landed=$?` prints `landed=0`. RED today: rc=1 for c52116840a against d60f277a26, 4baec37fdd and bcc23e3e02.
7. Pi: docs/workbench/TRACEABILITY.md gains ONE appended row under `## Tool feedback delivery receipts` naming the landed sha, the outside-clone command and `landed=0`; lines :222-230@b3f9890 stay byte-identical; the wb-cax.1 ledger validator exits 0.
8. Negative: no step edits HyperUnix source, tests, docs/feedback-dispositions.* or another writer's entry (README.md:93-94); `git show --stat <sha>` names no path outside the entry directory.

docs/workbench/TRACEABILITY.md:220-232 (append-only row; :226 byte-unchanged); wb-kqx notes (W20 channel record); external: HyperUnix-CLI new-feedback/2026-10-15-pi-workbench-sdk-find-preserves-incomplete-coverage-and-refuses-absence/ on origin/main.

description:
Gap (groomed by flywheel seat g1 round 1, run g2-work-r2; measured at rig origin/workbench/implementation-program 401b625 = BOUNDARY base at groom time; test anchors from git grep at the fetched tip):

docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md section "Adversarial test matrix" lists nine scenarios in one sentence: "Kill after Furnace side effect before returned Run ID; kill after workspace edit before recorded result; reconnect a stream with missing events; restart Pi while detached executor continues; change source digest under same logical key; issue control as observer-only; cancel a wait on shared child; exhaust Furnace slots with parents awaiting child; change candidate source basis after Forge verify." and binds them to one outcome sentence: "Required outcomes: reconciliation/uncertainty/conflict; no duplicate effects, no invented PASS, no implicit mass cancellation." docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md section "Truth labels and release gates": "Each major work package must have a falsifier: a negative test that would fail if a critical guarantee was quietly weakened." Cases embodying most scenarios exist at the tip, but NOTHING binds the nine scenarios to them: git grep -i 'adversarial test matrix|docs/workbench/08' over test/ names only three suites that cite docs/workbench/08 by another section (test/workbench-claude-cancel-faults.test.ts, test/workbench-furnace-evidence.test.ts, test/workflow-effect-replay.test.ts); wb-752.10 (in flight) binds the docs/09 controls, wb-gs2.2 (in flight) the docs/12 controls, wb-cax.23 pins the checklist-6/7 suites by PATH only. A rename, deletion or .skip of any embodying case leaves the docs/08 matrix claim intact with nothing red, and two scenarios may have no deterministic case at all, which today is invisible.

Candidate pins measured at 401b625 (EVIDENCE, not the table; the worker VERIFIES every title at the claim-time base): 1 Furnace effect before Run ID -> test/workbench-furnace-hosted.test.ts:384 "treats a timed-out or unreadable start as uncertain, closes the host, and refuses a blind second start" (wb-0kg.4, in flight, owns the Work-retry variant; reconnect alone cannot restore current without snapshot"; test/workbench-furnace-observer.test.ts:37 'reconnects only by fresh snapshot, marking a failed read stale instead of asserting last-known RUNNING'. 4 restart Pi while detached continues -> no deterministic case found by grep (exit|relaunch|reattach over test/workbench-local-detached*); fallback :182 "refuses absent/invalid caller, ABI and descriptor instead of producing a digest from partial input") and test/workbench-validate-reply.test.ts:190 "a digest mismatch is its own typed refusal, never a warning, and the core never runs". 6 observer-only control -> test/workbench-control.test.ts:86 "rule 2: observer-only grants cannot control under any action spelling, and nothing is read before refusing" and test/workbench-reconcile-decision.test.ts:71 "denies observer-only before any task lookup, identically for unknown and foreign tasks". 7 shared-child wait cancel -> wb-0kg.7 (in flight) owns the two-reader case; until it lands pin the no-implicit-mass-cancellation half: test/workbench-native-details.test.ts:104 "preserves selected node on resize and closes without invoking any runtime controls" and one it() inside test/workbench-furnace-control.test.ts:556 describe "observer stays zero-control; the adapter is the only control path", or record unpinned naming wb-0kg.7. 8 Furnace slot exhaustion -> no case at the tip (grep exhaust|slots over test/workbench-* finds only observation capacity bounds): unpinned with reason "no deterministic Furnace slot-exhaustion case; W09/W18 scope". 9 basis change after Forge verify -> test/workflow-effect-replay.test.ts:582 "never re-runs a journaled write because the basis changed", test/workbench-identity.test.ts:79 "never treats a mutable workspace path as an immutable source basis" and, for the no-invented-PASS half, test/workbench-forge-observer.test.ts:81 'F2: a current failed gate stays failed despite transport success, and current success is success'; title: W12 fault gap: a non-read node() leaves no journal row until it settles (runtime.ts appends only after await callNode), so a kill after the provider side effect but before the host result, or after the result but before the append, leaves nothing for the resume tripwire and the next resume re-runs the effect live (duplicate effect); record a dispatched row before the call so a resume refuses that position as uncertain-effect until an operator reconciles it
description:
Gap (groomed by flywheel seat g2 round 5, run g2-work-r1; measured at rig origin/workbench/implementation-program e830ac2 = BOUNDARY base at groom time; anchors from git show e830ac2:<path>):

src/workflow/runtime.ts records a node() journal row only when the call settles: the live path appends at :1509 (ok true) or :1533 (ok false), both AFTER `const output = await callNode({...})` (:1482); the only pre-settlement append is the carry-forward of an already-refused entry (:1417). The admission at :1305-:1313 treats `nodeJournal.get(index) === undefined` as `{ kind: "live" }`. journal.ts:213 documents "Append one settled call. Failure to write is not failure to run." and its header promises that for any non-read effect class "the resume stops on it rather than re-running or silently replaying an effect the previous run already performed." That tripwire exists only once a row exists. Consequence: a process kill (or host crash) between the provider side effect and the host result, or between the result and the append, leaves NO row at that position, so the next resume admits the position as live and performs the effect AGAIN — the duplicate effect docs/08 forbids. docs/14 names both locations as required fault-injection points and no test exercises them (grep over test/ for "before journal append|before host result|dispatched row" returns nothing; test/workflow-effect-replay.test.ts covers only recorded rows; wb-tu1 covers a recorded row with an absent class).

Scope (atomic; W12 side-effect policy; owner ruling requested on the row shape before claim, see notes):
1. Red first, test/workflow-effect-replay.test.ts: a fixture capability with a non-read effect class and an exactly-once effect counter; the host seam throws/kills after the effect counter increments but before the result reaches the runtime (location "after provider side effect but before host result"), and a second variant settles the result but fails the append (location "after result before journal append", journal append seam injected to throw once). Today the resume re-runs the node: the counter reaches 2. Quote the counter in the red note.
2. Fix shape (proposed, owner may reshape): immediately before `await callNode` (after nodeSemaphore.acquire and the aborted/settled check) and ONLY when the current effect class is not "read" (including an absent class, mirroring wb-tu1's fail-closed reading), append a dispatched row `{ kind: "node", index, key: key ?? "", ok: false, capabilityId, effectClass (when defined), basis, dispatched: true }` through the same recordJournal seam. The settled row at the same index supersedes it on read (nodeJournal is a Map built last-wins per index, runtime.ts:719-721), so a completed run resumes exactly as today. On resume a dispatched row with no settled successor is refused at :1313 as uncertain-effect (the existing non-read refusal), the workflow_node event carries reconcile.state "pending", the hint names the producer and position, and the row is carried forward verbatim; workflow_reconcile inspect reports the position with outcome "unrecorded" (dispatched, never settled). Read-class nodes write no pre-call row: journals of read-only and agent-only workflows stay byte-identical (existing journal fixtures and assertions untouched).
3. isEntry (journal.ts:229) accepts the optional `dispatched: true` marker (anything else drops the line as mangled, as today); journal-compat.ts MIRRORS the runtime (never re-implements): a dispatched row classifies node-effectful with the dispatched marker in its census and no new class unless the owner rules one; test/workflow-journal-compat.test.ts gains the mirror case. Reconcile acknowledge/override over a dispatched row bind by entryDigest exactly as over a failed row.
4. docs/workbench/08 "Side-effect replay policy on resume" gains one sentence naming the dispatched row (owner-authored or in the same commit per the owner's ruling) and TRACEABILITY gains the row; node qa/workbench/status-ledger.mjs --strict exits 0 before delivery (12:10Z seat rule).

Open questions for the owner (recorded in notes): Q1 marker shape (`dispatched: true` vs a failure-shaped row with no marker); Q2 whether a FAILED pre-call append on a non-read node refuses the call fail-closed or keeps journal.ts's "failure to write is not failure to run" (today's policy); Q3 whether the Claude host's settled-agent prefix needs the same pre-call row for agents with non-read gates (out of scope unless ruled in).

Non-scope: no change to read replay (same effect class, basis and key, marked stale), no change to the reconcile grants (never mint reconcile:*), no change to agent prefix semantics, no change to the admission order ("Decided synchronously, before anything yields"). description:
Gap (groomed by flywheel seat g2 round 5, run g2-work-r1; OWNER-DIRECTED filing per BOUNDARY 2026-10-15T13:30Z "wb-9x5.3 respin rulings": "F2 (real evidence channel, loadedPayload retired) + F3 wall-time p50/p95 = GROOM FILES a W21 follow-up bead (trunk >= ccb0fc8 harness), not blocked, not this respin." Measured at rig origin/workbench/implementation-program e830ac2 = BOUNDARY base at groom time; ccb0fc8 (wb-6ze.17, host-built EvidenceStore wired into the inspector dialog) is an ancestor of the tip.)

The wb-9x5.3 retained-memory receipt (in respin, gate cmd_b2e62ac8008d) proves post-GC retention bounds with payload bytes carried by a stand-in field (loadedPayload) that the inspector never reads (gate finding F2), and records neither bench wall time nor peak allocation (F3). Since ccb0fc8 the REAL evidence channel is on trunk: src/workbench/evidence-loader.ts EvidenceStore (request/get/abort/abortAll with {loaders; maxEntries; maxBytes; timeoutMs}), wired by the inspector dialog so Enter on a selected ref calls store.request, the details view renders from the synchronous store.get, and close calls abortAll. Nothing measures retained memory or wall time when large payload previews actually flow through that store under grouped-10k navigation.

Scope (atomic, measurement-only, src untouched, hot files untouched):
- qa/workbench/inspector-evidence-retained-bench.mjs (new; dist imports only; reuses qa/workbench/grouped-fixture.mjs): builds the grouped-10k fixture whose operation nodes list evidence refs, supplies a FIXTURE EvidenceLoader (fixture-named, never a real producer) whose load() returns bounded EvidenceContent previews derived from large payload buffers, constructs the EvidenceStore with header-stated bench-only budgets, and drives N navigation cycles through the SAME dialog/reducer path an operator uses: select node -> Enter (store.request) -> details render from store.get -> blur/selection change -> close (abortAll). Per cycle it records wall time (performance.now) and, after an explicit GC under --expose-gc at a header-stated warmup anchor, process.memoryUsage heapUsed/external; it reports p50/p95/max wall time, peak heapUsed between GCs, bytes offered vs bytes retained post-GC, loaded/aborted/unavailable entry counts, focusedCycles and detailsCycles judged equal to cycles (exit 2 otherwise, as ruled for wb-9x5.3 F1).
- Falsifiers in the same receipt: (a) release: after close/abortAll and GC, retained bytes attributable to evidence previews return to the stated floor and no loaded entry survives the store budget; (b) positive control: a deliberately retained payload reference is DETECTED as retained and released when dropped; (c) budget: the store never holds more than maxEntries entries or maxBytes preview bytes, and raw payload buffers are never reachable from a loaded entry (preview-only).
- Bounds (stated in the file header before any measurement, per the wb-9x5.4 bench rule bound at 13:05Z): retained-heap bound, wall-time bound, warmup anchor, bench-only limits (fixture size, maxEntries, maxBytes, timeoutMs) as constants with the disclosure "non-comparable to production (bench limits ... vs production ...)" copied into the receipt. A miss exits 1 and is recorded as a miss; off-shape exits 2; never a silent drop.
- Receipt: workbench.evidence-retained-bench/v1 to stdout and $W21_RECEIPT when set: utc, revision (git rev-parse HEAD + dirty flag), node, toolchain versions, host {platform, arch, cpus, model}, fixture, limits, bounds, cycles, series, outliers, verdict.
- test/workbench-evidence-retained-bench.test.ts: pins the header constants, the exit-code contract (0/1/2), the fixture-loader provenance label, the preview-only invariant and the positive-control detection on a tiny fixture (fast; no 10k run inside vitest).

src/workbench/attention.ts (wb-6ze.4) exports selectAttention(projection, input) (:267) over one query page (limit default 100, max 100: :68-69, :275), bottlenecks default 5 and max 20, a caller clock input.now (:27-28, validated :268-271), relation reads for the dependency-chain critical path, and an AttentionReport (:48-62) whose criticalPath is partial-estimated or incomplete-trace with reasons from the frozen ATTENTION_TRACE_REASONS (:21) and whose examined.truncated flags a cut page. wb-6ze.21 (open) renders the report in the overview and wb-6ze.36 (open) recomputes it on every projection revision change, so the report will be built on the live redraw path; its cost and its truncation behaviour at 10k grouped operations are unmeasured. The landed and in-flight receipts time other things: qa/workbench/inspector-grouped-bench.mjs layoutInspector (wb-9x5.1); wb-9x5.4 reducer updates and the inspector view-model selectors (per its notes it owns the docs/14 bullet "p50/p95 reducer update and UI selector time" for those selectors); wb-9x5.7 buildTimelineLanes; wb-9x5.10 buildGraphView; test/workbench-attention.test.ts is unit scale. The bench-only limits pin maxQuery 40 (qa/workbench/grouped-fixture.mjs:36 BENCH_ONLY_LIMITS) against attention's page of 100, so examined.truncated and the incomplete-trace reason truncated (:21) fire at a rate nobody has measured; this receipt measures it at maxQuery 40 and 100 (bench-only spread, never src).

Scope (atomic, measurement-only, hot-file free, no production limit or behaviour change):
- qa/workbench/attention-grouped-bench.mjs (new) over the compiled dist/ (npm run build first), reusing buildGroupedFixture, BENCH_ONLY_LIMITS, W21_SHAPE, assessFixtureShape, FIXTURE_EPOCH_MS and the GROUPED_FIXTURE_DEFAULTS/env overrides from qa/workbench/grouped-fixture.mjs exactly as inspector-grouped-bench.mjs does (:14-62). Never fork a second fixture or modify its exports.
- Two passes over one fixture: "maxQuery-40" with BENCH_ONLY_LIMITS as defined and "maxQuery-100" with {...BENCH_ONLY_LIMITS, maxQuery: 100} spread locally. Per pass: ingest the snapshots and relations, then sample selectAttention after every tick block while the fixture's 1..100-change ticks are applied (live churn, as wb-9x5.4 does), at least 1,000 samples per pass across bottlenecks {5, 20}; input.now is derived deterministically from FIXTURE_EPOCH_MS plus the tick index (never Date.now); a counting wrapper around the Pick<ObservationProjection, "query" | "relations"> input records query and relations calls and rows per report.
- Receipt (contract 'workbench.attention-grouped-bench/v1', one JSON line printed BEFORE the exit code is set, also written to $W21_ATTENTION_RECEIPT when set): utc, revision ($W21_REVISION else "working-tree"), node/arch/platform/cpus/cpuModel/toolchain, fixture shape {seed, nodes, depth, ticks, realised}; per pass and bottlenecks setting: build p50/p95/max ms; query and relations calls per report p50/max and rows per call max, with the count of reports where rows exceeded the page cap in force (must be 0); examined.truncated rate; criticalPath label rates and a histogram of incomplete-trace reasons over ATTENTION_TRACE_REASONS read from dist; counts series (active, waiting, stale, unknown, disconnected) p50/max; unmeasured and clockSkew p50/max; disconnectedProviders cardinality max; the 5 slowest samples with tick index and settings; pass flag.
- Exit codes mirror inspector-grouped-bench.mjs (:8-11): 0 measured at W21 shape with every judged p95 <= NAVIGATION_TARGET_MS (20); 1 measured but a judged p95 over target or a reads violation (a finding, recorded, never tuned away); 2 the measurement is not the W21 claim (fixture shape not realised or fewer than 1,000 samples); 3 nothing measured (exception on stderr, no receipt).
- test/workbench-attention-grouped-bench.test.ts (new, red-first): receipt assessor (field completeness, exit semantics including exit 2 on a fast off-shape receipt and exit 1 on an over-target pass), the timed function is the dist selectAttention with no Date.now or Math.random in the timed region and a fixture-derived now, production caps unchanged (observation.ts MAX_DEFAULT :93 and attention.ts DEFAULT_LIMIT / MAX_LIMIT / DEFAULT_BOTTLENECKS / MAX_BOTTLENECKS pinned by reading the source), Forge registration present.
- forge.toml: ONE additive block [build.commands.attention-grouped-bench] command "node qa/workbench/attention-grouped-bench.mjs" timeout 300, outside the default gate list. forge.toml is a 14e78f1-guarded file: declare it M in the delivery surface, remove no lines, and add no line equal to either non-blank line 14e78f1 added there ("[build.commands.inspector-grouped-bench]" and its command line), so the gate passes it under arm (b) of the BOUNDARY 2026-10-15T12:17Z two-arm rule. forge.toml is also a TRACEABILITY-cited file: run node qa/workbench/status-ledger.mjs --strict and require exit 0 before delivering (BOUNDARY 12:10Z/12:21Z seat rule).

Files: qa/workbench/attention-grouped-bench.mjs (new), test/workbench-attention-grouped-bench.test.ts (new), forge.toml (one command block). Out of scope: src/ (every file), grouped-fixture.mjs, inspector-grouped-bench.mjs, any production cap or default, wb-9x5.4's reducer and view-model measurements, wb-6ze.21/.36 rendering and wiring; the relationsPage adoption in attention.ts is wb-6ze.29. title: VC-6/W14: pure latency-decomposition selector over ObservationProjection source intervals (per-class union/busy ms for model/build/context/queue/query/host/other by frozen provider map; open or missing intervals counted, never summed; wall from the closed root interval else unknown; overhead only when every interval is closed and page complete; tokens unknown unless native usage given; MeasuredMetric rows for compareWorkflowRuns); designer.ts, attention.ts, wiring excluded
description:
Gap (groomed by flywheel seat g1 round 4, run g2-work-r1; measured at origin/workbench/implementation-program cd5aab7; src/workbench and src/index.ts are byte-identical at the b4ca4aa tip at filing; anchors from git show cd5aab7:<path>):

docs/workbench/09 section "Aggregates and profiling" requires latency decomposition derived "only with valid source intervals" and docs/workbench/11 section "Comparative experiment protocol" requires separating "model tokens, provider waiting, Forge build time, RF context time, external queue and overlay overhead when telemetry allows". Nothing in src/workbench computes any of it: git grep -i 'decompos\|latency' over src/workbench at cd5aab7 matches only a comment (capability-registry.ts:323). The projection already carries the inputs: ObservedNode.interval {startedAt, endedAt?} (observation.ts:10, :74), nativeRef.provider (:58), presentation.statusTone (:8), freshness and sourceConnectionState (:63-65), invocationId (:70); query() pages are bounded by maxQuery (default 100, :93) and report truncated. attention.ts (wb-6ze.4) measures OPEN intervals against a caller clock and a dependency-chain critical path; timeline.ts renders lanes; neither sums or attributes closed time by provider. designer.ts compareWorkflowRuns (:217) consumes CompareRun.metrics: readonly MeasuredMetric[] (:179, :185), but the registered workflow_compare tool fills metrics: [] (src/index.ts:2554), so every comparison today reports verdict unknown for want of a measured source (docs/11 section "Experimental read-only source tools": "Missing native measured metrics yields unknown, not a claimed optimization.").

Scope (atomic, pure, hot-file free): ONE new module src/workbench/latency.ts and ONE new test test/workbench-latency.test.ts.
- Export LATENCY_CONTRACT = "workbench.latency-decomposition/v1" (a new single-carrier literal; wb-cax.8's rule), a frozen LATENCY_CLASSES ["model", "build", "context", "queue", "query", "host", "other"] and a frozen provider map {claude-agent-sdk: model, forge: build, reactivefiber: context, furnace: queue, hyperunix: query, pi-workflow: host}; any other provider is "other" (never a guess from a title or kind).
- selectLatencyDecomposition(projection: Pick<ObservationProjection, "query">, input: {scope; invocationId; limit?: 1..100 default 100; usage?: readonly {source: NativeRef; inputTokens: number; outputTokens: number; evidenceRefs: readonly string[]}[]}) -> LatencyDecomposition {contract; basis: "observed"; invocationId; examined {nodes, truncated}; wall: {measured: true; ms; from: "root-interval"} | {measured: false; reasons}; components: one entry per class {class; providers (sorted, sanitized, bounded to 64 chars); nodes; intervals {closed, open, missing}; busyMs (sum of closed intervals); unionMs (union of closed intervals so concurrency never double-counts); measured: boolean; reasons}; waiting: {nodes; reasons: ["single-interval-per-node"]} (the projection holds one interval per node, so a waiting/executing split is unknown with that reason, never estimated); tokens: {measured: true; input; output; sources} only from supplied usage whose source matches an examined node's nativeRef, else {measured: false; reasons: ["no-native-usage"]}; overhead: {measured: true; ms} = wall minus the union of every component's closed intervals ONLY when wall is measured, examined.truncated is false and every examined interval is closed, else {measured: false; reasons}; caveat: one frozen constant stating closed source intervals only and unreconciled cross-provider clocks}. Reasons come from a frozen vocabulary (page-truncated, open-intervals, missing-intervals, no-root-interval, no-native-usage, single-interval-per-node).
- Export toMeasuredMetrics(report, {subjectBasis; freshness}) -> MeasuredMetric[] (designer.ts:179 shape; names latency.<class>.unionMs, latency.<class>.busyMs, latency.wall.ms, latency.overhead.ms; unit "ms"; source = the invocation's root nativeRef; coverage "complete" only when examined.truncated is false and the component's intervals.open + missing === 0, "partial" when some intervals are open or missing, "unknown" when nothing was measured; evidenceRefs from the examined nodes, bounded) so a caller can feed compareWorkflowRuns without any edit to designer.ts.
- Mirror attention.ts: refuse a bad limit with CapabilityError("validation", ...); re-check scope and invocationId on every page row (attention.ts:281); the wall comes from the examined node of presentation.type "workflow" for the invocation (the root) and only when its interval is closed; no clock, no Date.now, no Math.random; an interval whose instant is not a bounded timezone-qualified ISO-8601 string counts as missing; provider strings pass the shared sanitizers in src/workbench/redaction.ts (stripUnsafeText today; the single exported display helper once wb-952's respin lands) and a 64-char bound before they appear in output; no raw payloads, titles or evidence bodies in the report.

Non-scope: designer.ts, attention.ts, timeline.ts, observation.ts, src/index.ts and any Pi tool or dialog wiring (the workflow_compare reply builder is wb-69g.7; the metrics hookup into the registered tool is a later index.ts wiring bead under the BOUNDARY 12:25Z serialization rule); no estimate of a waiting/executing split; no critical path (attention.ts owns it); no token derivation from anything but supplied native usage.
acceptance_criteria:
All quotes are from docs/workbench in the rig at origin/workbench/implementation-program cd5aab7 (identical at b4ca4aa). Red-first: test/workbench-latency.test.ts fails before src/workbench/latency.ts exists.
L1. docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md section "Aggregates and profiling": "Distinguish measured actual from estimated projected metrics." and "Derive latency decomposition only with valid source intervals." -> only closed intervals (both bounds valid ISO instants) contribute to busyMs and unionMs; an open interval and a missing or malformed one are counted under intervals.open / intervals.missing and never summed; a static assertion proves the module source contains neither Date.now nor Math.random nor a now parameter.
L2. docs/workbench/11-designer-and-operator.md section "Comparative experiment protocol": "Separate model tokens, provider waiting, Forge build time, RF context time, external queue and overlay overhead when telemetry allows." -> a fixture with claude-agent-sdk, forge, reactivefiber, furnace and hyperunix nodes yields one component per class with providers listed, and unionMs < busyMs when two same-class intervals overlap; an unknown provider lands in "other"; waiting is reported with reason single-interval-per-node; tokens are measured only from supplied usage whose source matches an examined nativeRef (a usage row with a foreign source is ignored and the reason no-native-usage stands).
L3. docs/workbench/11 section "Comparative experiment protocol": "Decline precise claim if trace coverage insufficient; include raw evidence references." and section "Experimental read-only source tools": "Missing native measured metrics yields unknown, not a claimed optimization." -> overhead is measured only when wall is measured, examined.truncated is false and every examined interval is closed; a page larger than limit marks examined.truncated true, every component carries reason page-truncated and toMeasuredMetrics coverage is "partial" or "unknown", never "complete"; wall is unknown with reason no-root-interval when the root node has no closed interval.
L4. docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-038: "Versioned plan/execute/observe comparison uses immutable source and config digest references." and docs/workbench/15-implementation-program.md section "Vertical cuts" VC-6: "executes comparison with real native evidence; reports gains/confounders." -> toMeasuredMetrics rows satisfy designer.ts MeasuredMetric and, fed as CompareRun.metrics for a reference and a candidate run sharing one basis, compareWorkflowRuns reports the latency metrics as measured with reference and candidate summaries; with mismatched bases the existing confound behaviour is unchanged (designer.ts untouched, proven by git diff).
L5. Scope and bounds: a page row from another scope or invocation is dropped (attention.ts:281 precedent); a limit outside 1..100 is a typed CapabilityError validation refusal; the report for 100 nodes serialises under 8 KiB; provider strings carrying terminal escapes, bidi controls or zero-width characters are stripped and bounded through src/workbench/redaction.ts.
L6. Mutation table in the delivery note: summing open intervals, summing busy where union is reported, defaulting an unknown provider to model, measuring overhead on a truncated page, and minting tokens from node count each fail a named test.

(1..40, default 20), selectors? {tone, kind, relations, events {limit, after}}, maxBytes? (1024..65536, default 16384)} (:79-101), OBSERVE_CONTRACT "workbench.observe/v1", OBSERVE_DEFAULT_LIMIT, OBSERVE_MAX_LIMIT, OBSERVE_DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES, OBSERVE_MIN_MAX_BYTES, OBSERVE_MAX_MAX_BYTES, OBSERVE_CURSOR_MAX_BYTES (:34-43); cursors are bound to scope and revision and refused typed (CapabilityError "validation") when foreign, stale-above-revision or malformed; byte trimming emits truncatedForBytes + droppedForBytes, never silent. The docs/11 tool signature workflow_observe(ref, selectors?, cursor?, limit?) is therefore implemented as a pure module an operator or model cannot reach.

Scope (atomic, wiring only; claim only after wb-752.2 has LANDED on trunk): edit the workflow_observe registration in src/index.ts and add ONE new test file test/workbench-pi-observe.test.ts (boot the real extension in claude mode through test/helpers/boot-extension.ts, run a deterministic workflow, observe it through the registered tool).
- Parameters: taskId (unchanged), limit (integer; bounds from OBSERVE_MAX_LIMIT, never a spelled 40), cursor (string, maxLength from OBSERVE_CURSOR_MAX_BYTES), maxBytes (integer; bounds from OBSERVE_MIN_MAX_BYTES / OBSERVE_MAX_MAX_BYTES), selectors {tone?, kind?, relations?, events? {limit, after?}} mirroring ObserveSelectors.
- Order of checks preserved VERBATIM from today: workbench:observe grant ("Permission denied: workbench:observe grant required."), taskId regex ("Invalid workflow task ID."), task present and sessionId/workspace/principal match ("Workflow unavailable in this local operator/session/workspace scope."); only then observeInvocation(projection, {scope, invocationId: task.id, cursor, limit, selectors, maxBytes}).
- Reply text = sanitizeWorkbenchJsonText of {taskId, status, identity, inputDigest, workspaceSourceState, error (bounded + sanitized as today), ...ObserveReply}; the total never exceeds the requested maxBytes (default OBSERVE_DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES): pass the builder a maxBytes reduced by the measured size of the task-level envelope so truncatedForBytes/droppedForBytes stay the only truncation path. The builder's CapabilityError("validation") refusals (foreign/stale/malformed cursor, bad selectors, bad limit/maxBytes) become one typed sanitized tool text "Invalid observe request: <sanitized reason>" - never a stack, never a silent page restart.
- Nothing else in registerWorkbenchTools changes; observe-query.ts is imported, never edited; observation.ts untouched.
Excluded: observe-query.ts and observation.ts edits; the catalog/inspect wiring (sibling bead - same function, serialize); control wiring (owner-reserved wb-cra); furnace_observe; the dialog/inspector; docs beyond the TRACEABILITY landing paragraph.

Falsifiers (each a test case): F1 two pages over a >limit workflow: nextCursor round-trips, the union equals the window, a cursor from another task or another scope is refused typed; F2 kind and tone selectors return only matching nodes with window.scanned explaining the page; F3 selectors.relations counts relations without reading more than one page per node (reader spy); F4 projection.markStale on a running node -> freshness.summary names last-known-running + stale (string match on the builder's wording); F5 maxBytes at OBSERVE_MIN_MAX_BYTES -> reply bytes <= maxBytes, truncatedForBytes true, droppedForBytes reported; F6 the three legacy refusal texts are byte-identical to today's; F7 no spelled 20/40/16384/256 literal in the registration (source-text assertion over the tool block, constants imported).

Scope (atomic, additive, hot-file free): ONE new source file src/workbench/claude-control.ts and ONE new test file test/workbench-claude-control.test.ts. The adapter consumes a decideControl result for target.provider "claude-agent-sdk" plus an injected session seam -- an interface the adapter DEFINES and the host will later satisfy, e.g. `{ interrupt(session: NativeRef): Promise<SDKControlInterruptResponse | undefined> }`, fake in tests exactly like the injected invoke seam in src/workbench/providers/furnace.ts and the wb-69g.3 pattern. 1. Verb allowlist: the only executable verb is "interrupt", proven by importing NATIVE_CONTROL_ACTIONS["claude-agent-sdk"] (never spelling a second copy) and cited against sdk.d.ts:2882 in the delivery note (the BOUNDARY 09:16:19Z citation rule applied to this SDK); any other action for this provider is a typed refusal and the seam is never called.
2. Denied decisions (every ControlDenyPolicy, including "operator-confirmation" for the destructive interrupt and "missing-exact-grant" for a revoked control:claude-agent-sdk.interrupt grant) return a typed sanitized refusal; the seam call count is 0.
3. Permitted decision -> the seam is called exactly once with the receipt's target; the adapter never retries (park-not-retry): a seam rejection or timeout settles outcome "failed" (or stays "requested" when the rejection precedes any acknowledgment) with a redacted diagnostic category, never a second interrupt.
4. Acknowledgment echoes, never minted: a resolved SDKControlInterruptResponse becomes the acknowledged phase with nativeAckRef derived from the real receipt and the still_queued uuid COUNT (uuids themselves sanitized, never raw); an `undefined` resolution ("Older CLIs") acknowledges with a named no-receipt marker, never a fabricated uuid.
5. Transport success is never domain verification: a resolved interrupt never yields outcome "completed" or "cancelled" by itself; the result phase is settled only from an observed terminal supplied by the caller (projection), otherwise outcome "unknown" with the docs/06 uncertain wording.
6. Every string that can reach an operator (diagnostics, ack refs, refusal text) routes through the shared sanitizers in src/workbench/redaction.ts (strip, redact, strip); byte-bounded.
7. Audit: every receipt phase carries the ControlReceiptCore audit fields unchanged from the core (control.ts:40-54); the adapter adds nothing to and removes nothing from them.

Out of scope: Pi workflow_control registration (src/index.ts), host retention of the Query handle (claude-host.ts), live SDK or claude-live tier, control.ts edits, Furnace/local-detached/forge legs (wb-69g.3, wb-0kg.6).

Cycles/unknown dynamic edges represented explicitly as 'references' rather than rendered as a fake acyclic plan. Re-layout only changed neighborhood or viewport, not the complete graph for every event." and "## Rendering pipeline" requires "Graph layout cached by topology revision; no force-directed re-layout in render method. For large graphs show aggregate supernodes first." docs/10 "## Implemented experimental native details at 2026-10-15" confirms "Full graph/timeline navigation ... remain open."

Scope (atomic, pure, hot-file free; red-first): src/workbench/graph-view.ts (new, pure) exporting buildGraphView(reader, {scope, focus?, viewport, caps}) -> model with: cross-provider nodes (provider/type/status), typed edges carrying relation class and provenance source, fan-out beyond caps collapsed to counted aggregate supernode entries (shown first for large graphs), cycles and unknown dynamic edges returned as explicit reference entries (never silently broken into a fake acyclic plan), partial labels with counts whenever a RelationPage reports truncated (adopting wb-6ze.27 relationsPage; a truncated page is NEVER upgraded to complete), and revisionBasis {revision, topologyRevision}. Every label routes through the shared sanitizers in src/workbench/redaction.ts. test/workbench-graph-view.test.ts (new), red first.

Excluded: src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts and all rendering/wiring (hot for the owner wb-6ze.17 slice; graph-branch adoption is a follow-up that joins the wb-6ze.16/.21/.23/.26 workflow-inspector.ts serialization chain), the other hot files (src/ui/workflow-dialog.ts, src/ui/workflow-menu.ts, src/index.ts, src/workbench/evidence-wiring.ts), any production cap/limit change, any ObservationProjection mutation (read-only consumer).

title: defect(wb-g1g.2): topology slice silently undercounts remainder and labels trace observed when projection maxQuery (prod 40) is below requested relationPage (default 100)
description:
Found by flywheel adversarial review run g1-r3 of branch machine/flywheel/wb-g1g.2 (commit 54e4dcc, gate receipt cmd_87383785df8f, which carried this as finding topology-slice-silent-page-cap-undercount, CONFIRMED medium, ownerRulingNeeded).

Defect: selectLinkedTopology silently undercounts the remainder and mislabels the trace "observed" whenever the projection's own relation-page cap (ObservationLimits.maxQuery) is below the selector's requested relationPage (default 100).

Mechanism (verified in code at 54e4dcc): src/workbench/observation.ts:624-625 relations() clamps limit = Math.min(input.limit ?? maxQuery, maxQuery) and reports no truncation; src/workbench/topology-slice.ts readSide() computes full = rows.length >= page against the REQUESTED page, so a page clamped below the request is indistinguishable from a complete read. The only guard is a doc comment on TopologyCaps.relationPage ("Must not exceed the projection's own page cap") — nothing enforces it, and the DEFAULT (100) violates it for the production projection, which is constructed with maxQuery 40 (wb-6ze.27 description, measured at 24e6015: src/index.ts:2380; W21 bench qa/workbench/grouped-fixture.mjs:36 also pins 40).

Independent runtime reproduction (review worktree at 54e4dcc, real ObservationProjection, vitest): new ObservationProjection({maxQuery: 40}); 45 observed dependency edges F->n00..n44; selectLinkedTopology default caps returned downstream 10 listed, remainder {count: 30, atLeast: false}, trace {label: "observed", reasons: []}. Truth: 45 observed matching edges, so the true remainder is 35 — 5 observed edges silently dropped, the count claimed exact, and completeness claimed. Control: caps {relationPage: 40} correctly returns remainder.atLeast true and trace incomplete-trace with reasons ["relations-truncated"]. This corroborates the gate seat's probe (10 listed + remainder 30 atLeast false, trace observed, 40 of 45).

Why this refutes wb-g1g.2 acceptance: B3 "neighbors beyond caps collapse to a counted remainder, never silently dropped" and the bead title's "missing relations never fabricated, incomplete-trace labeled". A trace labeled "observed" with an exact-claimed remainder while observed matching edges are dropped is a fabricated completeness claim, reachable through the intended consumer path (wb-6ze.24 computes the slice from ObservationProjection typed relations; production maxQuery is 40).

Suggested fix (red-first): falsifier first — maxQuery-40 projection with 45 matching edges under DEFAULT caps must yield remainder.atLeast true and trace incomplete-trace/relations-truncated (or an exact count of 35). Then either (a) adopt relationsPage {relations, examined, truncated, limitApplied} once wb-6ze.27 lands (consumer adoption is explicitly excluded from wb-6ze.27's scope, so no other bead covers this) and treat truncated || limitApplied < requested as a full page, or (b) require/accept the projection's effective page cap from the caller and clamp the requested page to it. Existing behavior when the page is honored (rows.length >= page => atLeast + relations-truncated) is correct and must not regress; never weaken the delivered tests.

description:
Gap (measured 2026-10-15T10:40Z against origin/workbench/implementation-program 24e6015): two landed selectors compensate for relations() not reporting truncation. src/workbench/attention.ts:141-176 `observedEdges()` treats a page holding at least `whole = min(RELATION_PAGE 100, keys.length)` rows as possibly capped and re-reads it pair by pair (`projection.relations({scope, from: key, to, limit})` per examined key) under MAX_PAIR_READS = 2,000 (:75), setting `unread` when a pair page is itself full or the budget is spent; under production maxQuery 40 (src/index.ts:2380) with >= 40 examined nodes every node with >= 40 outgoing edges triggers up to keys.length extra reads. src/workbench/timeline.ts:362-363 reads `reader.relations({scope, to, limit: relationLimit})` per row and sets `relationsFull` only when `incoming.length >= relationLimit`; :44 records "relations() reports no truncation, so a page capped below this limit cannot be told from a complete one" -- a projection whose maxQuery is below the requested relationLimit (production 40 vs the 1..100 request range) cuts the page silently, the lane follows the cut page, and truncated.relations stays false with no 'relation-page-full' note. The sibling bead (blocked-by edge) adds `relationsPage(): {relations, examined, truncated, limitApplied}` to ObservationProjection; this bead makes the two selectors read the truth. The wb-6ze.6 gate relayed the gap as worker follow-up (3) and the Sr. Engineer approved the groom (BOUNDARY.md 10:23:58Z, 10:32:20Z).

Scope (atomic, two selector files, hot-file free, never less conservative than today):

- attention.ts: the `Projection` reader type gains OPTIONAL `relationsPage?`. When present, observedEdges reads `relationsPage({scope, from: key, limit: RELATION_PAGE})`; a page reported `truncated: false` is whole: no pair re-read and no budget spend; a page reported `truncated: true` follows today's path exactly (pair re-read within MAX_PAIR_READS, `unread` on a truncated or full pair page or a spent budget). When `relationsPage` is absent (legacy stand-ins, test/workbench-attention.test.ts:70 fake) behaviour is byte-identical to today. Report shape, the reasons vocabulary, `examined.truncated` (from query()) and the critical-path semantics are unchanged.
- timeline.ts: `TimelineReader` gains OPTIONAL `relationsPage?`. When present, the per-row read is `relationsPage({scope, to: row.observed.key, limit: relationLimit})` and `relationsFull ||= page.truncated || page.relations.length >= relationLimit` (a superset of today's rule, so test/workbench-timeline.test.ts acceptance 4 :527-553 pins stay green: an exactly-relationLimit page still flags). Lane assignment still uses only the first relationLimit rows read. When `relationsPage` is absent the model is byte-identical to today. Field name `truncated.relations` and the note 'relation-page-full' stay as they are (wb-6ze.26 renders them).
- No change to RELATION_PAGE, MAX_PAIR_READS, DEFAULT_RELATIONS, MAX_RELATIONS, MAX_ZOOM or any production limit.

Files: src/workbench/attention.ts, src/workbench/timeline.ts, test/workbench-attention.test.ts and test/workbench-timeline.test.ts (ADDITIVE cases only; or new test files test/workbench-attention-relations-page.test.ts and test/workbench-timeline-relations-page.test.ts). Existing cases, fakes and stand-ins stay untouched (they keep working through the optional fallback).

Out of scope: src/workbench/observation.ts (sibling bead); src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts relationsFor() :86-98 (wb-6ze.16/.21/.23/.26 serialization chain; those beads adopt RelationPage inside their own edits); wb-752.2 observe reply builder and wb-g1g.2 topology slice (in flight, they take relation rows from the caller); any hot file.

Falsifiers (mutation proof on a scratch copy, tabled in the delivery note): M1 attention skips the pair re-read even when truncated is true (hidden-remainder case :212-228 goes red); M2 attention treats a reported-truncated page below `whole` as whole (new capped-below-whole case goes red); M3 timeline drops the `>= relationLimit` half of the rule (acceptance-4 exact-page pin goes red); M4 timeline ignores `page.truncated` (new maxQuery-below-relationLimit case goes red); M5 legacy fallback removed (stand-in without relationsPage throws; byte-identical fallback case goes red).

Red-first: every new case is written against the base and observed failing (relationsPage ignored) before the selector change. Line anchors are at 24e6015.

B1 timeline tells a capped page from a complete one. docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md section "Four views" (Timeline): "Never infer exact timing from text or assume clocks agree; note uncertain clocks or event gaps." and section "Failure and deception defenses": "Historical reads with limited retention show missing details honestly." -- a projection constructed with {maxQuery: 2} holding 3 incoming ownership edges to one Attempt row, requested with relationLimit 40, yields truncated.relations true and notes containing 'relation-page-full' (today: false and absent); the same projection constructed with the default limits yields truncated.relations false and no note; lane assignment follows only the rows read.

B2 attention stops paying for whole pages. docs/workbench/10 section "Rendering pipeline": "Avoid O(allHistory) collapse per frame; maintain by-node last projection and ancestor aggregates incrementally." and docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md section "Performance benchmark": "no full 100k-event fold per redraw" -- 50 examined nodes each with exactly 50 outgoing dependency edges to examined nodes on a counting projection: with relationsPage present and every page reported whole, observedEdges issues exactly 50 relationsPage calls and 0 pair reads, and the AttentionReport deep-equals the report produced through the legacy path (relationsPage removed from the same projection object); with any page reported truncated the pair re-read count equals today's.

B3 hidden remainder stays reported. docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md section "Aggregates and profiling": "If dependencies or interval bounds are missing, suppress precise critical path claims and show incomplete trace." -- test/workbench-attention.test.ts:212-228 ("never misses an edge hidden behind a relation page the projection capped below the edges it holds") stays green byte-for-byte; a new case with maxQuery 2, three examined nodes and a page reported truncated below `whole` yields criticalPath label incomplete-trace with reason "truncated" in reasons, never a chain.

B4 never less conservative. docs/workbench/14 section "Truth labels and release gates": "Each major work package must have a falsifier: a negative test that would fail if a critical guarantee was quietly weakened." -- a brute-force falsifier over seeded random projections at maxQuery in {2, 5, 40, 100} compares the legacy path (relationsPage hidden) with the new path: attention `unread` and timeline `truncated.relations` are true on the new path whenever they are true on the legacy path; every AttentionReport field other than call counts is deep-equal; every TimelineModel field other than truncated.relations and the 'relation-page-full' note is deep-equal.

B5 legacy fallback byte-identical. docs/workbench/13-contracts-and-config.md is not quoted; the contract is wb-6ze.6's landed `TimelineReader = Pick<ObservationProjection,'window'|'relations'|'relationRevision'>` -- a reader stand-in without relationsPage (the a937f53 `loose` stand-in shape at test/workbench-timeline.test.ts:550-553) produces a TimelineModel deep-equal to the pre-change model over the existing fixtures A and the 1000-node acceptance-7 fixture; the attention fake at test/workbench-attention.test.ts:70 (query only) keeps producing deep-equal reports.

B6 contract fields unchanged for the renderers. docs/workbench/10 section "Four views" (Overview): "attention panel and top measured bottlenecks" and (Timeline) "relative interval lanes grouped by owner/phase/provider" -- TimelineModel keeps `truncated: {lanes, rows, relations, window}` and the frozen note vocabulary; AttentionReport keeps its contract string 'workbench.attention/v1', basis, counts and reasons; a snapshot of both type shapes (keys and note vocabulary) is pinned so wb-6ze.21 and wb-6ze.26 render the same fields.

B7 falsifiers and proof. Mutants M1-M5 from the description each turn exactly their named case red on a scratch copy while the base suite stays green; the delivery note tables mutant -> red test and the measured relations/relationsPage call counts for B2.

title: W14/VC-5: ObservationProjection reports relation-page truncation (new relationsPage returns {relations, examined, truncated, limitApplied} beside a byte-identical relations(); truncated only when a further MATCHING edge exists past the page, never from index size; cross-scope keys stay empty with examined 0; read-only, no revision change; mirrors the query()/events() shapes); consumer adoption and hot files excluded
description:
Gap (measured 2026-10-15T10:40Z against origin/workbench/implementation-program 24e6015, blobless clone, line anchors from `git show HEAD:<path>`): src/workbench/observation.ts:624 `relations(input: {scope; from?; to?; limit?}): Relation[]` clamps `limit = Math.min(input.limit ?? this.limits.maxQuery, this.limits.maxQuery)`, walks the outgoing/incoming/edgesByScope index and `break`s at the limit WITHOUT reporting it, while the sibling reads do report: `query()` (:704) returns `{nodes, examined, truncated}` and `events()` (:767) returns `{events, truncated, completeness}`. Production constructs the projection with maxQuery 40 (src/index.ts:2380, hot, not touched) and the W21 bench-only limits also pin maxQuery 40 (qa/workbench/grouped-fixture.mjs:36), while consumers request up to 100 (attention.ts:73 RELATION_PAGE = 100; workflow-inspector.ts:92-93 limit:100) or 40 (timeline.ts relationLimit default). Every consumer therefore guesses: attention.ts:141 "relations() reports no truncation and the projection caps each page at its own maxQuery, which this selector cannot see" and re-reads pair by pair under a 2,000-read budget (:75, :155-166); timeline.ts:44 "relations() reports no truncation, so a page capped below this limit cannot be told from a complete one" and :363 flags `truncated.relations` only when `incoming.length >= relationLimit`; workflow-inspector.ts:94-98 "a projection configured below 100 truncates silently, which relations() cannot report". Gate record: the wb-6ze.1 gate accepted "production maxQuery 40 < 100 makes relation-page truncation undetectable through relations(), so (partial) and relations partial fire only at 100"; the wb-6ze.6 gate relayed worker follow-up (3) "relations() reports no truncation, so a reader page cap below relationLimit cannot be detected". The Sr. Engineer approved this bead: BOUNDARY.md 2026-10-15T10:23:58Z "Approved for groom: ... relations() truncation-visibility bead" and 10:32:20Z "the four worker follow-ups are groom-approved".

Scope (atomic, additive, hot-file free): src/workbench/observation.ts plus ONE new test file.

- `export interface RelationPage { relations: Relation[]; examined: number; truncated: boolean; limitApplied: number }` and `relationsPage(input: {scope: ObservationScope; from?: string; to?: string; limit?: number}): RelationPage` on ObservationProjection. Same index selection as relations() (outgoing for `from`, incoming for `to`, edgesByScope otherwise), same scope-prefix guard, same exact from/to filters, same `Invalid relation query limit.` throw. `limitApplied = Math.min(input.limit ?? maxQuery, maxQuery)`. `examined` counts edges visited. `truncated` is true iff at least one further MATCHING edge exists beyond the returned rows: the walk looks one matching edge past the limit and stops. It never derives truncation from an index bucket's size, because a bucket may hold edges the exact from/to filter excludes.
- `relations()` keeps its signature and return type; it shares the private walk so `relations(input)` deep-equals `relationsPage(input).relations` for every input (falsifier below).
- Cross-scope `from`/`to` keys (prefix mismatch) return `{relations: [], examined: 0, truncated: false, limitApplied}` exactly as relations() returns `[]` today; a cross-scope caller learns nothing about edge counts.
- Read-only: `revision`, `topologyRevision`, indexes, edges and `stats()` are unchanged by any number of calls; no retained state is added.
- Export RelationPage so attention.ts, timeline.ts, the topology slice and the inspector can adopt it in follow-ups (a sibling adoption bead for attention.ts + timeline.ts is filed blocked-by this bead in the same groom round).

Files: src/workbench/observation.ts (additive method + exported type), test/workbench-observation-relations-page.test.ts (new). test/workbench-observation.test.ts may gain additive cases; its existing cases stay untouched.

Out of scope: consumer adoption (attention.ts, timeline.ts in the sibling bead; src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts relationsFor() :86-98 belongs to the wb-6ze.16/.21/.23/.26 serialization chain; wb-g1g.2 topology slice and wb-752.2 observe reply builder are in flight), any change to maxQuery or production limits, src/index.ts or any other hot file, Pi tool registration.

Falsifiers (mutation proof, run on a scratch copy and tabled in the delivery note): M1 `truncated := rows.length >= limit` (exact-limit page with no remainder must stay false); M2 `truncated := bucket.size > limit` ignoring the from/to filter (must stay false when the surplus is filtered out); M3 cross-scope key reports `examined > 0` (must stay 0); M4 relations() stops sharing the walk and diverges from `.relations` (deep-equal loop goes red); M5 relationsPage mutates revision (read-only case goes red).
acceptance_criteria:
All quotes are from docs/workbench in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program, base d180dbb or later; 24e6015 at groom time). Red-first: the new test file fails on the base (relationsPage absent) before src changes. Line anchors are at 24e6015.

A1 reported truncation. docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md section "Experimental projection implementation": "Query indexes cover native references, invocation, typed relations, source basis, status kind, evidence, version and intervals. Event queries expose metadata and references without raw producer payloads. Source-qualified cursor retention loss is explicitly partial-gap." -- a projection constructed with {maxQuery: 2} holding 3 outgoing edges from key A answers relationsPage({scope, from: A, limit: 100}) with relations.length 2, truncated true, limitApplied 2; with exactly 2 edges truncated is false; under maxQuery 100 with limit 3 and 3 edges truncated is false and limitApplied 3; a property loop over limits 1..5 x edge counts 0..5 x {from, to, scope-wide} asserts truncated === (matching > relations.length) and relations(input) deep-equals relationsPage(input).relations.

A2 filter-aware, never fabricated from the index. docs/workbench/09 section "Relationships are typed and provenanced": "Store edge provenance with timestamp and source; Graph view styles each differently. Missing edges do not imply independence." and docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md section "Four-view viewport increment": "Missing edges, timestamps and evidence loaders are visible unknowns, never fabricated." -- with 5 edges A->C and 1 edge A->B, relationsPage({scope, from: A, to: B, limit: 1}) returns the single A->B row with truncated false (the 5 unmatched bucket entries create no truncation) and examined >= 1; every returned row carries kind and a copied provenance {source, observedAt?, nativeConfirmationRef?} and mutating a returned row never changes a later read.

A3 brute-force falsifier. docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md section "Matrix by subsystem" Observation row: positive proof "snapshots, dedup, cursor resume, provenance", negative control "event loss -> stale and unknown" -- over a seeded random edge set (200+ edges, 5 kinds, 2 scopes, duplicate from/to pairs) and 500+ random queries, truncated equals (referenceMatchingCount > relations.length) in every case, relations.length <= limitApplied, and the returned rows are the first limitApplied matching rows in index order (the same order relations() returns today).

A4 scope boundary. docs/workbench/09 section "Data retention and privacy": "Tenant/workspace boundaries apply at correlation queries, not just at individual SDK calls." -- a from/to key of another workspace or principal yields {relations: [], examined: 0, truncated: false} and relations() yields []; a scope-wide page for scope B never includes a scope-A edge and reports truncation only from scope-B edges; the ownership edge of another scope is never counted toward truncation.

A5 bounded walk. docs/workbench/10 section "Rendering pipeline": "Avoid O(allHistory) collapse per frame; maintain by-node last projection and ancestor aggregates incrementally." -- for an indexed from/to query, examined <= (edges in that index bucket) and the walk stops after the first matching edge past the limit (examined <= position of that edge), never edges.size; `npm run build && node qa/workbench/inspector-bench.mjs` and `node qa/workbench/inspector-grouped-bench.mjs` still exit 0 with their receipts cited in the delivery note.

A6 read-only. docs/workbench/09 section "Two-layer storage model" item 2: "Workbench materializes a bounded, rebuildable read projection for UI and Pi tool queries. It can cache snapshots/events with source/provenance, but is not a second authoritative Run/Work/Attempt or a global DB mandatory for execution." -- stats(), relationRevision() and the query() revision are identical before and after any number of relationsPage calls; JSON.stringify(relationsPage(x)) is identical before and after relations(x); the method is absent from the ingest/refresh/relate/markStale/disconnect/reconnect mutation surface.

A7 falsifiers and proof. docs/workbench/14 section "Truth labels and release gates": "Each major work package must have a falsifier: a negative test that would fail if a critical guarantee was quietly weakened." -- mutants M1-M5 from the description each turn exactly their named case red on a scratch copy while the base suite stays green; the delivery note tables mutant -> red test; test/workbench-observation.test.ts, test/workbench-observation-aggregates.test.ts, test/workbench-attention.test.ts and test/workbench-timeline.test.ts stay green untouched.

The cancellation half is covered (wb-a2g.2 landed F1-F9 in test/workbench-claude-cancel-faults.test.ts; wb-a2g.1 is the live tier), absent credentials belong to wb-cax.5 (D1), invalid model to the live tiers (wb-a2g.1/wb-a2g.6), transcript privacy to wb-dc0.1 and resume negatives to test/workbench-host-contract.test.ts (L4 :113, :183, :197, :208). - :130-131 `if (!isAbsolute(config.cwd) || !existsSync(config.cwd)) return { ok: false, error: "Claude SDK cwd is inaccessible: ..." }` -- grep for "inaccessible" over test/ returns nothing.
- :235-236 `terminal.structured_output === undefined` with a declared schema -> "Claude SDK result is missing structured_output."; :238-239 `request.schema.check(...)` verdict !== true -> "Claude SDK structured output did not match schema: <verdict>" -- grep for either message over test/ returns nothing; the only structured_output fixtures are the success shapes at test/workbench-host-contract.test.ts:24 and :53.
- :229 success with no session id on init, assistant or result -> "Claude SDK succeeded without a session ID." -- untested.
- :83-91 `usage()` returns `{}` when `result.modelUsage` is absent or empty, so tokens/outputTokens stay ABSENT; docs/workbench/13 says "If the installed SDK lacks a field, omit it; no invented zeros or fake IDs." -- no test asserts absence (test/workbench-pi-client.test.ts:13 supplies modelUsage:{} but asserts nothing about tokens).
- :252-257 a throw from the SDK stream while the controller is NOT aborted -> `Claude SDK query failed: ${redactWorkbenchText(message)}` (ok:false, skipped absent) -- untested; the aborted branch (:254-255) is wb-a2g.2's F3/host-contract :134. Nothing pins that a credential inside the thrown SDK error is redacted before it reaches WorkflowSpawnResult.error.
- :199-212 the message loop recognizes exactly `system/init`, `assistant` and `result`; any other `type` is forwarded to onMessage and otherwise ignored, so a success-looking frame under an unknown discriminant must end as :216 "Claude SDK stream ended without a result message." (docs/workbench/13 "Key validations": "unrecognized SDK message version => diagnostic rather than silent success") -- untested; host-contract :152 covers only an empty tail.
- :226-228 a result with `subtype !== "success"` reports `redactWorkbenchText(terminal.errors.join("; ") || terminal.subtype)`, and `subtype === "success"` with `is_error: true` reports the redacted `result` text -- host-contract :123 covers one is_error shape; the error-subtype path, the empty errors[] fallback to the subtype label and the redaction of either text are unpinned.

comments.text: FINDING (ws-03, branch machine/flywheel/wb-a2g.7): the ~2.0 s is SDK-owned, NOT a Workbench wait. title: W15-D/VC-5: responsive pane composition in layoutInspector per docs/10 Layout responsiveness (single column below 80 cols or 20 rows unchanged; two panes view + selected details or timeline summary at 80-119; three panes hierarchy / graph-or-timeline / details at >=120 when viable, per-pane width and row caps; selection, focus and scroll intent survive resizes; visibleWidth-bounded in both tiers; one window per pane, no new loads); pure layout in workflow-inspector.ts only, wiring excluded
description:
Gap (measured 2026-10-15T09:48Z, rig checkout a67bc36, file unchanged at origin tip 4ca6bd5): docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md section "Layout responsiveness" specifies three geometry tiers — "<80 columns or <20 rows: single-column compact tree; details as subview, no side-by-side graph." / "80–119: two-pane tree + details or timeline summary; scrollable pane cap." / ">=120: left hierarchy, center graph/timeline, right details when viable; cap width and height." — and "Resize preserves node selection, focus and scroll intent where possible." Measured in src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts layoutInspector (lines 239-330+): the only width-dependent branch is `width>=80` guarding one "Selected ..." line (:301, :316); every view (overview/graph/timeline/details) renders ONE column at every width and height, so the 80-119 two-pane tier and the >=120 three-pane tier do not exist, while the <80/<20 tier is already satisfied by construction. test/workbench-inspector.test.ts asserts 80x24 and 120x40 renderings with toContain only (:22-:107), so a pane layout at >=120 can keep them green. Related beads cover adjacent but different ground: wb-cax.9 (test-only geometry conformance: width-bounded lines, resize without stale rows; no pane semantics), wb-9x5.1 (landed 4267c11: bench measuring layout cost at 80x24/120x40 and resize), wb-6ze.16 (details renders the topology slice), wb-6ze.21 (overview renders the attention panel). Store dedupe (pane/responsive/two-column/three-column/Layout responsiveness): no bead implements the tiers.

Scope (atomic): pure layout in src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts (layoutInspector and private helpers) plus tests; the key reducer handleInspectorKey and InspectorState are unchanged (Tab still cycles state.view; state.view selects the center pane content and which pane carries the pointer). Dialog/host wiring excluded (src/ui/workflow-dialog.ts is HOT and already passes {width, rows, ascii}). No new projection methods: each pane consumes the same single bounded window page the current code fetches (one projection.window per pane at most), never raw event history.

Pane rules to implement (literal reading of docs/10; the owner may re-rule pane assignment — record any ruling in the delivery note):
- width < 80 OR rows < 20: the existing single-column rendering, unchanged.
- 80 <= width < 120 AND rows >= 20: two panes separated by one column of the existing box glyph family (ASCII '|'): left = the state.view rows (tree for overview, blocks for graph, lanes for timeline); right = the selected node's details rows (the same rows the details view renders, including the landed evidence and topology rows) when a node is selected, else the timeline view's header/summary lines. Each pane has its own row cap equal to the shared body height; rows past the cap end with the existing "… N more row(s)" notice (never silently dropped); pane widths split the inner width with the left pane never narrower than 40 columns.
- width >= 120 AND rows >= 20: three panes — left hierarchy (overview tree), center graph when state.view is overview or graph else timeline lanes, right details — when viable, meaning each pane keeps a minimum width of 36 columns after two separators; otherwise fall back to the two-pane rule. Pane widths are capped (no pane wider than 80 columns; surplus is left blank) and the total line count never exceeds rows.
- The header lines (title/status, view/count/follow, filter, focus, rule) span the full width above the panes; the key-hint line stays the last row.

P1. Single-column tier unchanged. docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md section "Layout responsiveness": "<80 columns or <20 rows: single-column compact tree; details as subview, no side-by-side graph." -> for a fixture model with a selected node, layoutInspector at {width:79,rows:24}, {width:120,rows:19} and {width:30,rows:24} renders no pane separator and is byte-identical to the pre-change renderer's output captured in the red test for those geometries (the test pins today's lines for its own fixture, so the tier is proven unchanged rather than merely present).

P2. Two-pane tier. docs/workbench/10 section "Layout responsiveness": "80–119: two-pane tree + details or timeline summary; scrollable pane cap." -> at {width:80,rows:24} and {width:119,rows:40} with a selected node, every body row contains exactly one pane separator; the left pane holds the view rows (overview tree rows for view overview) and the right pane holds the selected node's details rows (native ref, status axes, evidence refs, and the landed topology rows from wb-6ze.16 when a slice is supplied); with no selection the right pane holds the timeline view's header/summary lines; a fixture with more rows than the pane budget renders the existing "… N more row(s)" notice inside the overflowing pane and never more than rows lines in total.

P3. Three-pane tier when viable. docs/workbench/10 section "Layout responsiveness": ">=120: left hierarchy, center graph/timeline, right details when viable; cap width and height." -> at {width:120,rows:40} with a selected node and view overview, body rows carry two separators: left = overview tree, center = graph blocks (the selected node's block first), right = details; with view timeline the center pane holds timeline lanes; at {width:200,rows:40} no pane exceeds 80 columns and no line exceeds 200 visible columns; at a width where three 36-column panes plus two separators do not fit the renderer falls back to the P2 two-pane rule (asserted at the boundary width computed from the exported minimums, which the test imports rather than restating).

P4. Resize preserves selection, focus and scroll intent. docs/workbench/10 section "Layout responsiveness": "Resize preserves node selection, focus and scroll intent where possible." -> the same InspectorState rendered at widths 79 -> 80 -> 120 -> 79 (rows 24/24/40/24) shows the pointer glyph on the same node ref in every geometry, keeps a focused subtree focused ("Focused on selected node and confirmed direct relations only" line present) and keeps the page offset (the "i/N" position in the view line) unchanged.

P5. Width safety in both tiers. docs/workbench/10 section "Layout responsiveness": "Unicode visibleWidth always used; guard wide CJK, combining emoji, ANSI codes, zero-width characters." and section "Proposed compact example": "For ASCII: +-|>, * running, x failed, ? unknown." -> with fixture titles containing CJK, combining emoji, embedded ANSI and zero-width characters, every emitted line has visibleWidth <= width at 80x24 and 120x40 in both the Unicode tier and {ascii:true}; the ASCII tier contains only ASCII separators and glyphs and no control bytes (shared sanitizer invariant).

P6. Bounded work, no new loads. docs/workbench/10 section "Rendering pipeline": "Avoid O(allHistory) collapse per frame; maintain by-node last projection and ancestor aggregates incrementally." and section "Four views" (Details): "Large content loaded only on focus." -> a projection spy records at most one window() call per rendered pane and zero calls to any event-history method during a three-pane render; no evidence loader or store.request is invoked by layoutInspector (store.get only, as today); the landed benchmark for wb-9x5.1 is re-run after the change and its measured p50/p95 at 80x24 and 120x40 are quoted in the delivery note (pass B stays within its own exit-1 rule; no production limit changes).

P7. Deception defenses preserved in every pane. docs/workbench/10 section "Failure and deception defenses": "STALLED vs WAITING vs STALE vs UNKNOWN must not be confused." -> the stale/unknown status text and the "Attention: stale/unknown is last-known state, not live progress." / critical-path lines (or the wb-6ze.21 attention panel when an AttentionReport is supplied) remain present in the overview pane at 80x24 and 120x40; tones and freshness labels are rendered identically to the single-column tier for the same node.

P8. Scope discipline: src diff touches only src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts; handleInspectorKey and InspectorState unchanged; dialog/host wiring untouched; all existing inspector tests and the wb-g1g.1/wb-6ze.16/wb-6ze.21 pins pass verbatim; biome clean; no any; no inline imports.
