Gap: docs/workbench/15 names "native immutable deployment refs" as VC-7 acceptance and docs/workbench/08 says native executable identity is an unestablished release obligation; W18 (wb-5w0) notes "Native binaries ... not claimed" and W22 (wb-cax) notes "Full release/install native binary identity ... remain open". At rig ad3cf6e the detached host hard-codes `nativeRuntimeIdentity: "unsupported"` (src/workbench/hosts/local-detached.ts:82 and :96) and its runtimeClosure comment reads "Native executables launched by SDK defaults/PATH still have unsupported identity."; src/workbench/providers/forge.ts:80 launches ServerConnection.spawn("forge"), a bare PATH-resolved name; the Claude Agent SDK's Options.pathToClaudeCodeExecutable (node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts:1984) "Uses the built-in executable if not specified." Nothing in src/ can observe, pin or compare the bytes of a native executable, so no host can honestly report which binary it launched or refuse reattachment when that binary changed.

Scope (atomic, pure, hot-file free): ONE new source file src/workbench/executable-identity.ts and ONE new test file test/workbench-executable-identity.test.ts; wire nothing.
- export const EXECUTABLE_IDENTITY_CONTRACT = 'workbench.executable-identity/v1'
- export type ExecutableIdentityReason = 'sdk-default-executable' | 'not-found' | 'not-a-file' | 'not-executable' | 'symlink-depth' | 'too-large' | 'unreadable' | 'path-resolved' | 'shadowed-candidates' | 'search-truncated' (frozen set; nothing else is ever emitted).
- export interface ExecutableObservation { contractVersion: typeof EXECUTABLE_IDENTITY_CONTRACT; requested: string | undefined; resolution: 'absolute' | 'path-search' | 'unresolved'; resolvedPath?: string; realPath?: string; symlinkHops: number; digest?: string (sha256:<hex>); sizeBytes?: number; mode?: number; candidates: number; immutability: 'digest-observed' | 'mutable-path' | 'unsupported'; reasons: readonly ExecutableIdentityReason[]; observedAt: string }
- export function observeExecutableIdentity(input: { command: string | undefined; cwd: string; path: string | undefined; observedAt: string; maxBytes?: number; maxSearchEntries?: number; maxSymlinkHops?: number }): ExecutableObservation — synchronous; reads only through node:fs (lstat, readlink, stat, chunked reads for hashing — never readFileSync of a whole binary); never imports node:child_process; never reads process.env (PATH is an explicit input); never throws for a missing, unreadable, non-regular, non-executable or oversized target — those are 'unresolved'/'unsupported' with a reason.
  • command undefined or empty -> resolution 'unresolved', immutability 'unsupported', reasons ['sdk-default-executable'] (the honest answer for the Claude built-in executable and any SDK default).
  • command containing a path separator -> resolved against cwd; symlinks followed hop by hop (count hops; above maxSymlinkHops, default 16, -> 'unsupported' with 'symlink-depth'); must be a regular file with an execute bit; hashed with sha256 when sizeBytes <= maxBytes (default 512 MiB) -> resolution 'absolute', immutability 'digest-observed'; oversize -> digest omitted, immutability 'unsupported', reasons ['too-large'].
  • bare command -> PATH searched in order (split on path.delimiter; at most maxSearchEntries, default 64, further entries ignored and 'search-truncated' recorded; relative or empty entries resolved against cwd); the first regular executable file wins; candidates counts every searched entry holding a same-named executable; resolution 'path-search'; the digest IS observed but immutability is 'mutable-path' with reasons ['path-resolved'] plus 'shadowed-candidates' when candidates > 1. A digest never upgrades a PATH-resolved binary to 'digest-observed'.
  • Result and its reasons are frozen; resolvedPath and realPath pass through redactWorkbenchText (paths may embed tokens); absent fields mean not observed, never a default.
- export function compareExecutableIdentity(recorded: ExecutableObservation, current: ExecutableObservation): { verdict: 'same' | 'changed' | 'unknown'; differences: readonly string[] } — 'same' only when both digests are present and equal AND both immutability values are 'digest-observed'; 'changed' when both digests are present and differ; otherwise 'unknown' (a mutable-path or unsupported side can never yield 'same'); differences names each differing field (digest, realPath, sizeBytes, mode, immutability, resolution).

Out of scope: editing src/workbench/hosts/local-detached.ts (in flight under wb-6hb.1; the 'unsupported' literal is W18's later wiring point), src/workbench/providers/forge.ts, src/workbench/claude-host.ts, src/workbench/identity.ts; discovering the Claude built-in executable path from SDK internals; remote host authentication; Furnace ExecutorApp. If acceptance cannot be met without touching a hot or reserved file, stop and return blocked.

Files: src/workbench/executable-identity.ts (new); test/workbench-executable-identity.test.ts (new; mkdtemp fixtures with explicit modes only; nothing is executed). Imports: node:fs, node:path, node:crypto; redactWorkbenchText from src/workbench/redaction.ts (hot, import only). Specs: docs/workbench/08 (Separate four identities; Experimental immutable receipt; Optional local detached profile; Run recovery and journal design), docs/workbench/17 (Versioning / distribution), docs/workbench/12 (Supply chain; Credential boundaries), docs/workbench/15 (Vertical cuts VC-7), docs/workbench/02 WB-014/WB-041.
acceptance_criteria:
All criteria quote docs/workbench specs in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program, HEAD ad3cf6e). Red-first: test/workbench-executable-identity.test.ts fails before src/workbench/executable-identity.ts exists. All fixtures live under a mkdtemp directory with explicit modes; nothing is executed.

B1. docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md section "Separate four identities": "2. Deployment: immutable digest of artifact, dependencies, configuration and compatible host ABI." -> for a fixture file written with mode 0o755 and referenced by absolute path, observeExecutableIdentity returns resolution 'absolute', immutability 'digest-observed', digest equal to 'sha256:' plus the hex sha256 of the same bytes, sizeBytes equal to the byte length, symlinkHops 0, candidates 1 and reasons []; observing process.execPath by absolute path also yields 'digest-observed', and two observations of it are deep-equal apart from observedAt.

B2. docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md section "Experimental immutable receipt": "A model alias, mutable PATH or SDK default executable must not be advertised as an immutable native deployment merely because the JavaScript client is pinned." -> the bare name 'forge' (the literal src/workbench/providers/forge.ts:80 spawns) with a PATH of two temp directories each holding an executable 'forge' resolves to the FIRST directory with resolution 'path-search', candidates 2, immutability 'mutable-path' and reasons containing 'path-resolved' and 'shadowed-candidates' although digest is present; reversing the PATH order changes realPath and digest; command undefined yields resolution 'unresolved', immutability 'unsupported', reasons ['sdk-default-executable'] and no digest.

B3. docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md section "Experimental immutable receipt": "The identity audit also pins explicitly resolved loaded SDK JavaScript files, rather than assuming a lockfile/archive proves the installed bytes." -> a symlink chain link2 -> link1 -> binary yields realPath equal to the binary's realpath, symlinkHops 2 and the same digest as the direct observation; a chain longer than maxSymlinkHops yields immutability 'unsupported' with reasons ['symlink-depth'] and no digest; a mode 0o644 file as the only PATH candidate yields resolution 'unresolved' with reasons ['not-executable']; a directory named like the command yields 'not-a-file'; a missing command yields 'not-found'; none of these throws.

B4. docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md section "Run recovery and journal design": "Do not silently migrate a running invocation to new source/registry version." and docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md section "Versioning / distribution": "Pin immutable deploy artifact for reproducible observations." -> compareExecutableIdentity returns verdict 'same' for two digest-observed observations of identical bytes even when observedAt differs; 'changed' with differences including 'digest' after one byte of the fixture is rewritten; and 'unknown' whenever either side lacks a digest or is 'mutable-path' or 'unsupported' — a mutable-path pair with equal digests is 'unknown', never 'same'.

B5. docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md section "Optional local detached profile": "Furnace-hosted durability and native executable identity are separate, unestablished release obligations." and docs/workbench/15-implementation-program.md section "Vertical cuts" VC-7: "Remote host authentication, reattachment, native immutable deployment refs, crash/uncertain-operation conformance." -> the module's own source, read by the test, contains none of 'node:child_process', 'process.env' or 'Date.now'; a 64-byte fixture observed with maxBytes 16 yields 'unsupported' with reasons ['too-large'] and no digest; the observation, its reasons array and the comparison result are frozen and JSON round-trip stable.

B6. docs/workbench/12-security.md section "Supply chain": "Pin SDK versions, package/artifact digests and provenance." and section "Credential boundaries": "redact tokens from logs, UI, recordings and failure messages." -> a PATH entry whose directory name contains 'Bearer abc123' never appears raw in resolvedPath, realPath or reasons (the redactWorkbenchText marker replaces it); a PATH with 100 entries and the match only in entry 90 is searched for at most maxSearchEntries (64) and reports resolution 'unresolved' with reasons containing 'search-truncated' rather than a certain 'not-found'.

B7. docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-014: "Workflow invocation carries definition, immutable implementation basis and logical invocation ID; native refs remain intact." and WB-041: "Optional detached workbench host permits Pi client disconnect/reconnect, without falsely claiming crash durability." -> contractVersion is exactly 'workbench.executable-identity/v1' on every observation; the whole suite runs with no TTY, no spawned process and no network; test/workbench-local-detached.test.ts stays green and git diff --name-only shows only the two new files.

Process: red-first; ./node_modules/.bin/biome check --write on both files; no any; no inline imports; never weaken or delete existing tests; forge run lint / typing / test green in the worktree; hot and reserved files untouched; do not edit docs/TRACEABILITY.md.
notes:
Sr. Engineer constraint 2026-10-15: observation only, never executes any binary; digest claims only for absolute immutable paths; PATH-resolved stays mutable-path; SDK-default stays unsupported; reattach comparison never upgrades unknown to same. Base e797a84+.
2026-10-15 gate-2 (g2-gate-r1) VERDICT PASS: complete gate cmd_d357964c4b62 on machine/flywheel/wb-0kg.2 @ 3ab693c (tree 546969c, base 0f3a067; merge-tree onto b44f1ce clean, no overlap, refined 14e78f1 merge-base check 4/4 equal). 167 files, 3022 passed, 1 expected fail, 7 skipped; red reproduced (module absent) and green 34/34; owner constraints met, 10/10 targeted mutants killed. Proposed closure in the outbox. Owner note: B4 vs description ambiguity (mutable-path side with a differing digest yields changed, never same) stated as finding F4 in the summary.

[flywheel relay of Sr. Engineer rulings, 2026-10-15 ~13:40Z] F4 RULING (binds the comparison semantics): a mutable path whose digests differ is "changed" (fail-closed is correct); "unknown" is reserved for a missing or unreadable digest on either side; "same" requires equal digests. The delivered behaviour matches this ruling. F3 (carry into W18 wiring, owner-policy, no bead yet): an identity capture must resolve the ELF behind a wrapper (realpath of /proc/self/exe or the resolved interpreter), never pin process.execPath verbatim — on this host process.execPath is a mise bash wrapper. F5/F6: standing invariants hold (renderers sanitize; digest decides), no action. F7 accepted as UNDETERMINED with the worker's disclosure. skipIf(ROOT_USER) markers accepted. Pre-verified by the owner (tip/surface/merge-tree af4c865); lands serially right after the owner's b67b2ed push.

title: VC-7/W18-A: detached-host fault-injection conformance tier (effect-then-crash before host result, SIGTERM on a running owned host, cancel isolation across two hosts, shutdown unresolvedEffects) with exactly-once effect markers and an evidence-grade receipt; measurement-only, dist imports, src untouched
description:
Gap (measured at rig HEAD ad3cf6e908f0): VC-7 (wb-0kg) names "crash/uncertain-operation conformance" and has no decomposition bead; W18 (wb-5w0) notes claim "unknown no retry afterloss" from qa/workbench/local-detached-client.mjs (cmd_b21303c30b15), which kills a host DURING a provider wait (SIGKILL) and inspects after a graceful shutdown, proving inspect() -> unknown + reconcileHint, execute() rejection and same-id relaunch conflict. Nothing kills the host AFTER a provider side effect has happened but BEFORE the host records the result (docs/workbench/14 § "Fault-injection locations": "after provider side effect but before host result"); nothing proves the effect happened exactly once and is never repeated through reattach, execute or relaunch; nothing shows that cancelling one host leaves a sibling host running ("no implicit mass cancellation"); and the shutdown reply's unresolvedEffects flag (src/workbench/hosts/local-detached.ts connectDetachedWorkflow().shutdown -> { accepted, unresolvedEffects }) is never asserted. TRACEABILITY WB-026 and WB-041 stay fixture/experimental.

Scope (atomic, measurement-only, hot-file free; src/ untouched: src/workbench/hosts/local-detached.ts is reserved by wb-6hb.1 and only its compiled dist/ output is driven here):
1. qa/workbench/local-detached-faults-receipt.mjs (new, pure, no src/ or dist/ import): faultProviderSource({ capabilityId, markerDirectory, crashAfterEffect }) returning the ESM text of a trusted-local provider (effectClass "write", permissions ["fixture:effect"], contractSource "fixture:source") whose invoke(input, ctx) appends one marker file "<markerDirectory>/<ctx.invocationId>.<n>" (the irreversible effect) and, when crashAfterEffect is true, calls process.kill(process.pid, "SIGKILL") synchronously BEFORE returning so the host never records a result; assessFaultJourneys(observed) -> { findings: {rule, detail}[], realised: boolean }; buildFaultReceipt(input) -> frozen { contract: "workbench.detached-faults/v1", utc, revision, node, arch, platform, journeys, markerCounts, findings, realised, pass }.
2. qa/workbench/local-detached-faults.mjs (new runner; imports ../../dist/workbench/hosts/local-detached.js exactly like qa/workbench/local-detached-client.mjs plus node: builtins; mkdtemp workspace mode 0700 with the provider module, helper and marker directory inside it; every host SIGTERMed and the directory removed in finally):
   F1 effect-then-crash: launch invocation "effect-crash" with the crashing provider (grants ["fixture:effect"], localProvider manifest with the module digest, permissions ["inspect", "execute"]); poll inspect() until terminal "unknown"; then execute() must reject, launchDetachedWorkflow with the same invocationId must reject /exists|conflict/, and the marker count for "effect-crash" must be exactly 1 after all three; then launch "effect-crash-second" (an explicit NEW logical invocation with the same input) and record that it is accepted and writes its own single marker (total 2 across two ids, labelled explicitSecondRequest).
   F2 cancel isolation: launch "iso-a" and "iso-b" with a non-crashing wait provider (ms 10000); cancel "iso-a" with a bounded reason; record accepted/terminalConfirmed; poll "iso-a" to terminal "cancelled"; inspect "iso-b": observation "observed-running" or "observed-started", terminal undefined, cancellationRequested false, controlAudit empty; then shutdown both.
   F3 shutdown with unresolved effects: launch "unresolved" (wait 10000, running) and "idle" (autoStart false, never executed); shutdown both; record unresolvedEffects true for "unresolved" and false for "idle"; inspect "unresolved" afterwards -> terminal "unknown" with reconcileHint, never "completed".
   F4 SIGTERM on an owned running host "sigterm": process.kill(pid, "SIGTERM"); poll inspect() -> terminal "unknown"; execute() rejects; marker count unchanged.
   Each journey records timestamps and the measured latency from kill/cancel to the first unknown/cancelled observation.
3. Exit semantics (receipt printed as one JSON line and written to $DETACHED_FAULTS_RECEIPT when set, BEFORE exiting): 0 = realised and no findings; 1 = realised with findings (a measured violation, recorded honestly); 2 = not realised (non-Linux or setuid operator per localOperator(), missing dist/ build, or the crashing provider did not terminate the host within 5 s) with a diagnostic.
4. forge.toml: one additive [build.commands.local-detached-faults] block (command "node qa/workbench/local-detached-faults.mjs", timeout 240), NOT added to the default [build] gate list (same placement as local-detached-shell).
5. test/workbench-detached-faults-receipt.test.ts (new vitest, offline): imports the pure module; asserts the generated provider text registers the given capabilityId with effectClass "write", writes the marker before the kill, contains process.kill(process.pid, "SIGKILL") only when crashAfterEffect, and never imports node:net or node:child_process; runs the assessor negative fixtures in the acceptance; reads qa/workbench/local-detached-faults.mjs as text and asserts it imports only ../../dist/workbench/hosts/local-detached.js and node: builtins.

Out of scope: editing src/workbench/hosts/local-detached.ts or any src/ file (if a journey measures a violation - a replayed effect, a sibling cancelled, a fabricated terminal verdict - record the finding in the ledger line and bead notes and return blocked); remote authentication, other-UID negatives, Furnace ExecutorApp hosting and native binary identity (each needs live hosts or the reserved file); W12 effect-metadata refusal on resume (lands with wb-6hb.1; a follow-up extends this tier to assert the typed uncertain-effect once describeNodeEffect exists); editing qa/workbench/local-detached-client.mjs; editing docs/TRACEABILITY.md.

Files: qa/workbench/local-detached-faults-receipt.mjs (new), qa/workbench/local-detached-faults.mjs (new), test/workbench-detached-faults-receipt.test.ts (new), forge.toml (one additive block).
acceptance_criteria:
Red-first: test/workbench-detached-faults-receipt.test.ts fails before qa/workbench/local-detached-faults-receipt.mjs exists. All quotes are from docs/workbench in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program).

D1. An effect that happened is never repeated and never reported as a verdict. In F1 the marker count for "effect-crash" is exactly 1 after the crash, after inspect() reports terminal "unknown" (observation "unknown", source "local-client-transport", reconcileHint matching /never.*retry|do not.*retry/i, no result field), after execute() rejected and after the same-id relaunch rejected /exists|conflict/; the snapshot never reports terminal "completed" or "failed" for that invocation. Quote docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "Adversarial test matrix": "Kill after Furnace side effect before returned Run ID; kill after workspace edit before recorded result; ... Required outcomes: reconciliation/uncertainty/conflict; no duplicate effects, no invented PASS, no implicit mass cancellation." Quote docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "Optional local detached profile": "Inspection after host loss reports unknown with producer reconciliation guidance; it does not replay a saved terminal verdict or rerun JavaScript." Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-026: "Interrupted effectful operation is reconciled through producer or marked uncertain; no automatic blind repeat."

D2. A lost result is not evidence the effect did not happen. The F1 receipt records effectObserved true (the marker exists) together with terminal "unknown", and the assessor records finding "effect-denied" if any journey field claims the effect did not occur. Quote docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "State/event semantics": "An observed timeout or disconnect is *not* evidence that side effect never happened." Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md § "Nonfunctional invariants" NFR-02: "No host auto-retry of ambiguous irreversible writes."

D3. A deliberate second request is a new logical invocation, not a retry. "effect-crash-second" is accepted, writes exactly one marker of its own, and the receipt labels it explicitSecondRequest true with totalMarkers 2 across two ids; a relaunch under the ORIGINAL id stays refused. Quote docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "Separate four identities": "Logical invocation: caller-created unique identity stable across retry of same request; distinct from identical intentional second request." Quote docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md § "Runtime and host requirements": "A Pi UI reconnect is only an observer/client action; it must not restart external work."

D4. Cancellation has three phases and touches one host. In F2 cancel() returns { accepted: true, terminalConfirmed: false }; the next inspect() of "iso-a" shows cancellationRequested true before terminal "cancelled" appears; "iso-b" keeps observation "observed-running" or "observed-started", terminal undefined, cancellationRequested false and controlAudit [] throughout, and ends only by its own shutdown command. Quote docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "State/event semantics": "Cancellation request != accepted cancellation != terminal cancellation." Quote docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "Cancellation and ownership": "Multi-reader shared child MUST NOT be stopped merely because one reader closed Pi or stopped waiting." Quote docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Fault-injection locations": "Concurrent readers with one shared child; stopping one reader must not stop child without ownership."

D5. Shutdown reports unresolved effects honestly. In F3 shutdown of the running "unresolved" host returns unresolvedEffects true and of the never-executed "idle" host returns unresolvedEffects false; the later inspect() of "unresolved" is terminal "unknown" with a reconcileHint, never "completed". Quote docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md § "Runtime and host requirements": "Shutdown: stop accepting calls, notify owned local tasks, attempt graceful end, report unresolved effects, and release owned resources." Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-041: "Optional detached workbench host permits Pi client disconnect/reconnect, without falsely claiming crash durability."

D6. SIGTERM is loss, not completion. In F4 inspect() after SIGTERM reaches terminal "unknown" within 5 s (latency recorded), execute() rejects, and the marker count is unchanged. Quote docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "Lifetimes": "Detached service: independent process survives Pi client disconnect but does not guarantee service crash recovery." Quote docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md § "Current experimental distribution": "The local detached shell tier is a separate process-lifecycle proof, not remote authentication or native crash-durability evidence."

D7. Offline falsifiers in test/workbench-detached-faults-receipt.test.ts: a journey with marker count 2 under one id -> finding "duplicate-effect"; terminal "completed" after crash -> finding "fabricated-terminal"; same-id relaunch accepted -> finding "reuse-after-loss"; sibling cancellationRequested true or terminal "cancelled" -> finding "mass-cancellation"; unresolvedEffects false for a running host -> finding "unresolved-effects-hidden"; a clean fixture -> pass true with every receipt field present; the generated provider text contains exactly one marker write before process.kill and none after. Quote docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Truth labels and release gates": "Each major work package must have a falsifier: a negative test that would fail if a critical guarantee was quietly weakened." Quote docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Test classes" D: "Fault: ambiguous write timeout, process kill at every side-effect boundary, transport disconnect".

D8. Evidence-grade receipt and placement. The receipt carries contract "workbench.detached-faults/v1", utc, revision (git rev-parse HEAD or the literal "working-tree"), node, arch, platform, per-journey timestamps and latencies, markerCounts, findings, realised and pass, and contains no absolute filesystem path (basenames and invocation ids only); forge.toml gains exactly one [build.commands.local-detached-faults] block (command "node qa/workbench/local-detached-faults.mjs", timeout 240) with the [build] gate list byte-for-byte unchanged (the test asserts both); npm run build && forge run local-detached-faults is executed in the worktree and its command id, exit code and receipt are recorded in the delivered ledger line; node qa/workbench/local-detached-client.mjs still exits 0. Quote docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Truth labels and release gates": "Every test evidence artifact includes revision, tool versions, commands, timestamp, host, native references and actual output." Quote docs/workbench/15-implementation-program.md § "Vertical cuts" VC-7: "Remote host authentication, reattachment, native immutable deployment refs, crash/uncertain-operation conformance."

D9. Gate. ./node_modules/.bin/biome check --write on the new test; npm run typecheck clean (no any, no inline imports); ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run test/workbench-detached-faults-receipt.test.ts test/workbench-local-detached.test.ts green; src/ unchanged (git diff --name-only shows no src/ path); never weaken or delete existing tests; do not edit docs/TRACEABILITY.md (acceptance owner reconciles).

title: VC-6 residual: unify definition.schemaVersion literal across detached host and embedded receipts

title: W22-C: offline vendored native-SDK pin falsifier (vendor/README.md SHA-256 table == tarball bytes; package-lock file:vendor entries carry inBundle+integrity+matching version; bundledDependencies covers every file:vendor dependency; no orphan tarball)
description:
Gap: vendor/README.md publishes SHA-256 values for forge-sdk-0.1.0.tgz, furnace-sdk-0.1.0.tgz and hyperunix-sdk-0.1.0.tgz as a prose table. src/workbench/identity.ts verifies package-lock integrity against vendor bytes at invocation-identity capture time (test "pins actual package.json, package-lock.json and local vendor artifact bytes"), but nothing in the portable gate checks that (a) the README table equals the on-disk SHA-256 of each tarball, (b) every `file:vendor/*.tgz` dependency in package.json is listed in `bundledDependencies` and has a package-lock `packages["node_modules/<name>"]` entry with `resolved: "file:vendor/<file>"`, `inBundle: true`, a version matching the tarball filename and a well-formed integrity, or (c) no tarball exists without a README row and a package.json dependency (orphan). docs/workbench/TRACEABILITY.md § "Clean external install" records the real regression this guards: cmd_8d6d9f378d88 failed because "npm could not resolve local native SDK tarballs before extracting the parent package" until the SDKs were bundled; today that would only be caught by the network-requiring install-smoke tier.

Deliver: test/workbench-vendor-pins.test.ts (new vitest; node:crypto sha256 over vendor/*.tgz; parses the README markdown table rows `| <file> | <sha256> |`, package.json and package-lock.json; no network, no npm child process). Implement the checker as a pure function inside the test file (input: { readmeRows, tarballDigests, manifest, lock }, output: string[] of findings) so the same function runs against the real tree AND against in-memory negative fixtures: a README row with one hex digit changed -> finding naming the file and both digests; a `file:vendor/x.tgz` dependency absent from bundledDependencies -> finding; a lock entry with `inBundle: false` or a `resolved` that is not `file:vendor/<file>` -> finding; a tarball without a README row or without a package.json dependency -> orphan finding; a version in the filename that differs from the lock entry version -> finding.

Out of scope: changing vendor contents, versions, lockfile or package.json (if the real-tree run is red at rig HEAD, stop, record the mismatch in the ledger line and return blocked rather than editing pins); docs edits; src/ edits; forge.toml edits.

Files: test/workbench-vendor-pins.test.ts (new).
acceptance_criteria:
All criteria quote docs/workbench specs or vendor/README.md in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program).

2. docs/workbench/12-security.md § "Supply chain": "Pin SDK versions, package/artifact digests and provenance." -> an in-memory fixture whose README digest differs by one hex digit yields a finding that names the file and both digests; a tarball with no README row, or no package.json dependency, yields an orphan finding; a filename/lock version disagreement yields a finding.
3. docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Truth labels and release gates": "Pin dependencies, lockfile and package exports." and docs/workbench/TRACEABILITY.md § "Clean external install": "npm could not resolve local native SDK tarballs before extracting the parent package." -> a fixture with a `file:vendor/` dependency absent from bundledDependencies, or whose lock entry has inBundle false, yields a finding; the test runs inside `npm run test` (portable gate) with no network and no npm child process.

They do not establish that the producing checkouts were clean or that every native runtime supports every SDK method." and docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "Experimental immutable receipt": "Native executable identity remains a producer-specific observation." -> assertion messages and test names say the artifact BYTES are pinned and make no claim about native executables or clean producer checkouts.

title: VC-6/W17-A: pure digest-pinned workflow patch proposal (bounded redacted diff, static validation of the candidate, affected pinned invocations stay unchanged, operator-only promotion receipt; never writes source or replaces a running invocation); Pi tool registration excluded
description:
Gap: src/workbench/designer.ts (hot; import-only here) ships catalogWorkflows / inspectWorkflowSource / validateWorkflowSource and the measured-cohort compareWorkflowRuns, but nothing represents designer-cycle steps C ("DESIGN a source edit and corresponding validation plan"), D ("CHECK compile/types, SDK permission bindings and expected side effects") and H ("REPORT diff ... Human/operator promotes changes explicitly") for a CANDIDATE source. docs/workbench/TRACEABILITY.md lists WB-038, WB-039 and WB-047 as "planned" with no source or test. The VC-6 journey "Pi generates a source diff improving redundant task, validates it, executes reproducible comparison and cites native results" has no artifact between "generate a diff" and "validate".

Deliver ONE new pure module and ONE new test file; register nothing; edit no existing file.

src/workbench/patch-proposal.ts (new; imports only: type WorkflowSource, type WorkflowValidation, validateWorkflowSource from ./designer.js; type DefinitionRef, type InvocationSnapshot, canonicalJson, identityDigest from ./identity.js; type CapabilityRegistry from ./capability-registry.js; redactWorkbenchText from ./redaction.js; safeWorkflowTerminalText from ../ui/workflow-card.js; createHash from node:crypto. Nothing from node:fs, node:child_process or any provider):
• PATCH_PROPOSAL_CONTRACT = "workbench.patch-proposal/v1"; class PatchProposalError extends Error { code: "SOURCE_DIGEST_MISMATCH" | "CANDIDATE_TOO_LARGE" | "PROMOTION_PRECONDITION" | "VALIDATION" }.
• proposeWorkflowPatch(input: { base: WorkflowSource; candidateSource: string; rationale: string; hypothesis?: { metric: string; direction: "lower" | "higher"; groundedIn: readonly string[] }; pinnedInvocations?: readonly InvocationSnapshot[]; registry?: CapabilityRegistry; grants?: readonly string[]; limits?: { maxDiffLines?: number; maxPreviewBytes?: number } }): WorkflowPatchProposal.
  – First check: base.definition.artifactDigest must equal `sha256:<hex>` of base.source (same form designer.ts uses) else throw PatchProposalError("SOURCE_DIGEST_MISMATCH") before any diff or validation work.
  – candidate.definition = { ...base.definition, artifactDigest: sha256(candidateSource) }; validation = validateWorkflowSource({ definition: candidate.definition, sourceRef: base.sourceRef, source: candidateSource }, { registry, grants }) so SOURCE_TOO_LARGE, control-character, META and possible-call/grant diagnostics are inherited unchanged and `executed` stays false.
  – diff: deterministic line diff (LCS or Myers) over base vs candidate; hunks `{ op: "context" | "add" | "remove"; baseLine?: number; candidateLine?: number; text: string }` with text = safeWorkflowTerminalText(redactWorkbenchText(line)); bounded by limits.maxDiffLines (default 400) and limits.maxPreviewBytes (default 65536) with `truncated: boolean`; `summary: { added, removed, unchanged }` counted over the FULL diff even when the preview is truncated; identical bytes -> status "no-change" with zero hunks.
  – affectedPinnedInvocations: for each pinnedInvocations entry whose scriptDigest === base.definition.artifactDigest -> { logicalInvocationId, scriptDigest, action: "unchanged", note: "remains pinned to the base digest; the candidate requires a new logical invocation" }; other snapshots are only counted in unrelatedInvocations; input snapshots are never mutated.
  – promotion: { state: "proposed"; requires: "operator"; applied: false }; experiment: { independentVariable: "source"; referenceDigest; candidateDigest; mustHold: ["inputDigest", "modelDigest", "toolsDigest", "environmentDigest", "cacheDigest"] } (the CompareRun field names, so compareWorkflowRuns can later treat source as the only intended difference); hypothesis echoed with grounding: "ungrounded" when groundedIn is empty; causalClaim: false; status: validation.status ("valid" | "invalid" | "uncertain") or "no-change"; contractVersion; proposalDigest = identityDigest("patch-proposal", <proposal without proposalDigest>).
  – Every returned object is deep-frozen plain data; JSON round-trip is lossless.
• recordPromotionDecision(proposal, decision: { decision: "promoted" | "rejected" | "deferred"; principal: { id: string; role?: string }; at: string; reason: string }): PromotionReceipt — frozen; "promoted" requires proposal.status === "valid" else throw PatchProposalError("PROMOTION_PRECONDITION"); receipt fields: contractVersion, proposalDigest, decision, principal, at, reason, appliesTo: "versioned-source", appliedByWorkbench: false, pinnedInvocationsChanged: 0. The module exports no function that accepts a filesystem path.

test/workbench-patch-proposal.test.ts (new): red-first; no TTY, provider, network or filesystem writes; uses an in-memory WorkflowSource built like test/workbench-designer.test.ts does, an InvocationSnapshot fixture from captureInvocationIdentity (identity.ts) or a literal, and a stub CapabilityRegistry for the grant case.

Out of scope: editing src/workbench/designer.ts, src/index.ts, src/workbench/redaction.ts, src/ui/workflow-card.ts or any other existing/hot file; registering a Pi tool (workflow_propose would live in hot src/index.ts); applying patches; executing candidates; comparing runs (compareWorkflowRuns exists). If the worker finds an edit to an existing file necessary to satisfy acceptance, stop and return blocked.

6. docs/workbench/11-designer-and-operator.md § "Workflow designer cycle": "H. REPORT diff, tests, effect assumptions, realized improvement and residual uncertainty. Human/operator promotes changes explicitly." -> recordPromotionDecision returns a frozen receipt with contractVersion, proposalDigest (identityDigest over the proposal), decision, principal, at, reason, appliesTo "versioned-source", appliedByWorkbench false, pinnedInvocationsChanged 0; "promoted" on an "invalid", "uncertain" or "no-change" proposal throws PROMOTION_PRECONDITION; a hypothesis with empty groundedIn reports grounding "ungrounded"; causalClaim is false everywhere and no field named gain, improvement or speedup exists.
7. docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-030: "Layout, reducers, status classification and control capabilities are pure/testable without a real terminal." and docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Matrix by subsystem" Designer row: "reproducible before/after with native references | changed model/basis flagged as confound" -> the whole suite runs with no TTY, provider or network; two calls with identical inputs produce deep-equal proposals (including proposalDigest); JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(proposal)) deep-equals proposal; Object.isFrozen holds for the proposal, its hunks array and the receipt.

description:

Scope (atomic, hot-file free, no docs edits):
- qa/workbench/status-ledger.mjs (new; no src/ or dist/ import) exporting parseLedger(markdown) -> { header: string[]; rows: LedgerRow[]; cmdTokens: string[] } and validateLedger(parsed, { root, allowedStatuses }) -> { integrity: Finding[]; vocabulary: Finding[] } where Finding = { rule, row?, detail }, plus a CLI: node qa/workbench/status-ledger.mjs [--strict] [--doc docs/workbench/TRACEABILITY.md] printing a JSON receipt {contract:'workbench.status-ledger/v1', utc, revision (git rev-parse HEAD or 'working-tree'), rows, statusCounts, integrity, vocabulary, strict, pass} to stdout and to $W22_LEDGER_RECEIPT when set. Exit 0 when integrity is empty (vocabulary findings are reported only); exit 1 when integrity is non-empty, or when --strict and vocabulary is non-empty; exit 2 when the table header does not match exactly: ID | Priority | Requirement | Implementation evidence | L1 shell | L2 client | L3 integration | L4 unit/fault | Live/native evidence | Status.

- Vocabulary rule (strict only): Status is in the allowlist = the words named by docs/workbench/02 NFR-08 and IMPLEMENTATION_GUIDE rule 10 (shipped, experimental, planned, blocked, fixture) plus the literals present today (gate-pass, live-sdk, source-retained); anything else is a vocabulary finding naming the row.

title: W21-A: deterministic nested-group 10k swarm fixture + bounded grouped projection/inspector benchmark receipt (no cap raise)
description:
Build the measurement harness W21 needs BEFORE any node-cap or aggregation decision. The projection (src/workbench/observation.ts store()) FIFO-evicts the oldest node once maxNodes (default 2000) is reached, so a 10k-operation swarm is silently truncated today; this bead measures that honestly rather than hiding it or raising caps.

Deliver three artifacts, nothing else:
1. test/helpers/swarm-fixture.ts — a deterministic (seeded, no Date.now()/Math.random() in the measured path) generator that yields: >=10,000 `sdk-operation` nodes under 5-level nested `group` nodes joined by `grouping` relations; partial `dependency` and `hypothesis` links (not every node linked); long Unicode titles (CJK, combining marks); large payloadRef strings; and a tick stream of 1-100 active status changes per tick totalling >=100,000 ObservationEvents, all under one invocationId and one ObservationScope. Mixed providers (forge/furnace/claude-agent-sdk) with colliding numeric ids to exercise provider-qualified keys.
2. qa/workbench/grouped-bench.mjs (dist/ imports, same shape as qa/workbench/inspector-bench.mjs) plus a `[build.commands.grouped-bench]` entry in forge.toml: ingest the fixture into `new ObservationProjection()` with DEFAULT limits (maxNodes 2000, maxEdges 4000 — do not raise), then take 1000 keyboard navigation + layoutInspector samples cycling overview/graph/timeline/details at 80x24, 120x40 and ASCII tier, plus resize samples (80x24 <-> 120x40), and write a JSON receipt (W21_BENCH_RECEIPT env path, like W15_BENCH_RECEIPT).
3. test/workbench-grouped-bench.test.ts — vitest guard: two generations of the fixture are deep-equal; group depth is exactly 5; operations >= 10,000; events >= 100,000; ticks have 1..100 changes; the receipt shape has every field named in the acceptance; and a falsifier that fails if the bench projection is constructed with maxNodes > 2000 or maxEdges > 4000.

Out of scope (separate follow-up beads): raising caps, adding ancestor/supernode aggregation to observation.ts or workflow-inspector.ts, dialog wiring, any hot file. Do not modify qa/workbench/inspector-bench.mjs or test/workbench-observation-perf.test.ts.
acceptance_criteria:

title: HXFS-PI-R4: Pi files the hx install-skill target vs Pi skill-loader root disjointness upstream (W20)
description:
## Statement
The hyper-unix skill installer writes to no directory that Pi's skill loader reads: `hx install-skill` targets `~/.skills/hyper-unix` and nine agent homes (`~/.claude/skills`, `~/.kiro/skills`, `~/.codex/skills`, `~/.hermes/skills`, `~/.config/opencode/skills`, `~/.grok/skills`, `~/.qwen/skills`, `~/.gemini/skills`, `~/.cursor/skills`) while Pi resolves `skills:` from `<cwd>/.pi/skills`, `<cwd>/.agents/skills`, `~/.pi/agent/skills`, `~/.agents/skills`, `~/.pi/skills`; a Pi-backend hosted agent declaring `skills: hyper-unix` therefore receives the not-found placeholder after a successful `hx install-skill`. Resolution is sibling-side (an install target whose marker is `~/.pi/`) or, alternatively, a Pi loader root at the marker-free default `~/.skills`; the request travels Pi's upstream-feedback channel (wb-kqx). Pi's leg is limited to filing that request; adopting the alternative loader root is a design option, not a requirement. obligationOn: sibling (HyperUnix-CLI).

## Rationale
Facts CONFIRMED by both lenses: complete ten-row target table at HyperUnix-CLI:src/hx_cli/cmd_skill.ml:20-64@d60f277a26, confirmed by skill/hyper-unix/SKILL.md:23-27; Pi roots at Pi-subagents:src/skill-loader.ts:41-47@b3f9890 with the placeholder at :52; intersection empty by static reading (`git grep -n -E '\.pi/agent|\.pi/skills|\.agents/skills' d60f277a26 -- src skill docs sdk` -> no match). Corrected annotation: `const settings = config.settingSources ?? [];` (src/workbench/claude-host.ts:127@b3f9890) means the Claude backend reads `~/.claude/skills` only when an operator sets settingSources to include `user`, so by default both backends miss the install. HXFS G7 (02-charter-and-ownership.md:21) keeps HX independent of consumers, so adding a target is HX's own design surface; Pi's rule routes the finding upstream rather than into a shim (docs/workbench/15-implementation-program.md:81@b3f9890). Contested: the NOT-AN-OBLIGATION-ON-PI refuter rules the filing discretionary under the wb-kqx convention (no text binds Pi; Pi nowhere promises the skill); seat resolution: obligationOn sibling stands, the Pi leg is the discretionary W20 filing the channel exists for, at bd 3, and the alternative loader root is explicitly not required.

## Acceptance criteria
1. A feedback entry is filed in HyperUnix-CLI `new-feedback/` per README.md@d60f277a26 conventions (metadata block; the claim graded CONFIRMED with both target tables quoted at d60f277a26 and b3f9890; the positive beside it: Claude-backend sessions configured with settingSources including `user` do reach `~/.claude/skills`), landed on origin/main with `landed=0` from an outside clone, `tools/lint/feedback-layout.sh` exit 0, and the vendor-name grep over the commit printing nothing. 2. Sibling landing falsifier (either branch satisfies): `hx install-skill --list` shows a row whose skills_dir resolves inside one of Pi's five roots (e.g. `~/.pi/agent/skills` with marker `~/.pi/`), OR Pi's loader adds `join(homedir(), ".skills")`; in either case a Pi vitest runs `HOME=$TMP hx install-skill`, then `preloadSkills(['hyper-unix'], cwd)` returns content beginning with the SKILL.md frontmatter `name: hyper-unix` (SKILL.md:1-4) instead of the :52 placeholder. RED today under both repos as pinned.
3. Negative kept: Pi's loader still rejects symlinked roots/dirs/SKILL.md (skill-loader.ts:18,:56,:85) and never hand-edits or copies the installed bundle (a hand copy carries no `.hx-skill-receipt.json` and is classified `foreign` by `hx install-skill --check`, skill/hyper-unix/references/workspace.md:463,:540-543). title: FURNACE-PI-R2: Furnace reply readers tolerate additive members and refuse missing required ones (fixtures)
description:
## Statement
Pi-subagents' Furnace reply readers (run status, attempt list, logs read, run inspect, run start record) shall keep accepting a reply that carries additive unknown members beside the members they require (per-verb `kind` check plus required-field presence/type checks, never an exact key-set check), and a hermetic fixture shall feed one unknown top-level member and one unknown nested member through each reader and assert the produced reading is unchanged while a missing required member still refuses.

## Rationale
The duty is verbatim and addressed to clients: "| `FRN-PRO-002` | Forward field tolerance | Clients MUST be able to ignore additive fields within the same compatible protocol version. | `contract` |" (Furnace:docs/initial-setup/02-atomic-requirements.md:162@8f20e9bb8), with FRN-PRO-012 (:172, unknown event tolerance SHOULD) and the Furnace-side half ("Where an existing command gains optional graph references, additions must follow the existing protocol's compatibility policy." 12-migration-and-compatibility.md:152; "Do not silently add required FOH fields to existing unrelated JSON objects." :150; FRN-XP-012). Additive growth is recorded practice: the response-kind count pin moved 24 -> 25 for the additive `query_answer` kind (existing-test-amendments.md:126), and the pin range already adds an optional member to a DTO Pi reads (`RunStatusDto.attention_explained_by`). Pi complies by construction (kind checks at furnace-observer.ts:89-94, furnace-evidence.ts:175, providers/furnace.ts:19-24, furnace-hosted.ts:221; no Object.keys over the four reader files at b3f9890) — but only the logs-read leg is pinned (wb-6ze.8's fixture, test/workbench-furnace-evidence.test.ts:239-254). Without a pin for the other four, a later "tighten the shape check" change (compare wb-2j3.9's eight-key strictness on the RF envelope) could break Pi the day Furnace lands an optional reference. Grade: CONFIRMED (dossier seat re-read FRN-PRO-002 at 8f20e9bb8; Lens 1 kept PLAUSIBLE on the compatibility-policy inference, which bears on urgency, not binding). Priority: P0 by rubric; proposer suggested bd 4 (test-only, no behaviour change), recorded here as 3, the floor of the filing schema's 0-3 range. Fold alternative: wb-6hb.11 docs-07 census or wb-cax.27 docs-16 compatibility census instead of this bead.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Unit, hermetic, fake-client fixtures already used by the three furnace test files (and the inspect provider's test): for each of the five readers, a reply equal to the existing green fixture plus `{"graph_ref":{"relation":"x"}}` at the top level of `data` and one unknown member inside one nested object (an attempt item for attempt list; the `record` object for run inspect and run start; the run object for run status; the logs `data` object's non-line members for logs read) produces a reading deep-equal (`toStrictEqual`) to the fixture's reading — observer: the FurnaceReading; evidence: the evidence record content; inspect: the returned source; hosted: `{ run, beadsRunId, requestId }`.
2. The same reply with one required member removed — `run.workspace` (status), the attempt list's run identity, `log.attempt_id` (logs read), `record.run_id` (inspect), `started.record.run_id` (start) — still throws the existing CapabilityError category (`unavailable` or `authorization` as each reader throws today at b3f9890); `expect(...).rejects.toMatchObject({ category })`.
3. The logs-read leg reuses wb-6ze.8's fixture at test/workbench-furnace-evidence.test.ts:239-254 (already feeds additive top-level members) and ADDS the nested-member case rather than duplicating it; its malformed-shape table (:396) already covers the missing-required half.
4. Source census (pattern test/workbench-surface-census.test.ts): none of src/workbench/furnace-observer.ts, furnace-evidence.ts, providers/furnace.ts, hosts/furnace-hosted.ts matches an `Object.keys(...).length` guard or compares a key set against a literal list; in src/ the kind checks remain per-verb string equalities.
5. GREEN: no behaviour change; fixtures and census land. If folded into wb-6hb.11, the docs/07 Furnace section first gains the tolerance sentence the census binds. Out-of-scope guard: never apply the wb-2j3.9 strictness pattern (RF-envelope-specific) to a Furnace reply reader — it would violate FRN-PRO-002.

All @b3f9890.

title: FURNACE-PI-R1: hosted adapter keeps an all-false DurabilityProfile; hermetic test pins the hello wire claim
description:
## Statement
Pi-subagents' Furnace-hosted adapter shall keep registering its executor with no durability declaration, so the bridge host's hello reply advertises a `DurabilityProfile` with every member false (the executor claims no resolve/reattach/checkpoint/restore/replay/cancel-continuity capability), and a hermetic test shall assert on the captured hello reply that the executor's `durability` object has exactly the nine profile members and every value false, beside the receipt's `limits.crashDurability: "none"`.

## Rationale
CONFIRMED mechanism duty (furnace dossier Verdict 3, FHFD-PI-1; proposer, Lens 1 and Lens 2 agree). Routing is decided by the advertised profile: "a durable operation is sent only to an executor whose valid profile sets that member to true; an absent profile reads every member false (part 2)." (Furnace:executor-protocol/registry/durability-profile-rules.json:2@8f20e9bb8); "An executor without `durability` claims nothing: every member reads false (`FRN-DUR-008`)." docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md section "Rendering pipeline" states nine bullets, verbatim: (1) "Event burst coalescing (e.g. <=4 ordinary updates/s while active), not every token update." (2) "Seconds-only clock tick <=1Hz and only for visible running rows." (3) "No 80ms whole-dialog refresh under large-workload mode." (4) "Pure layout and keyboard reducers are unit-tested without a TTY." (5) "Avoid O(allHistory) collapse per frame; maintain by-node last projection and ancestor aggregates incrementally." (6) "Virtualized visible rows + modest overscan; expensive Markdown syntax parsing only for selected transcript slice." (7) "Graph layout cached by topology revision; no force-directed re-layout in render method. For large graphs show aggregate supernodes first." (8) "Bound memory: store highlights/current snapshots; stream older event/traces lazily." (9) "Pi observation tools paginate/filter/limit and return compact JSON, never rendered ANSI." docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md "Truth labels and release gates": "Each major work package must have a falsifier: a negative test that would fail if a critical guarantee was quietly weakened." docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md section "Failure and deception defenses" states five honesty defenses verbatim: "STALLED vs WAITING vs STALE vs UNKNOWN must not be confused. Spinner should not imply work progressed. Node result with missing evidence is not marked verified merely because process exited 0. Cancel controls unavailable for observers without lifecycle authority. Historical reads with limited retention show missing details honestly." docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md section "Truth labels and release gates" requires "Each major work package must have a falsifier: a negative test that would fail if a critical guarantee was quietly weakened."

Cases embodying each defense exist at the tip, but NOTHING binds the five sentences to them: grep -i 'deception|docs/10' over test/ names no mapping (the docs/09 and docs/11 censuses bind other lists), so a rename, deletion or .skip of any of them leaves the docs/10 claim intact with nothing red. Non-scope: no change to what the suites assert about git behaviour. description: Gap (owner, measured 2026-10-15 ~11:20Z on the gate host): /tmp is a tmpfs with 1,048,576 inodes and sat at 94% inode use; forge refused the owner gate before lint started (FORGE_STEP_SCRATCH_EXHAUSTED: 67,104 inodes free under the 131,072 floor; command_id cmd_0b678b8dce46). title: wb-g1g.1 review: evidence preview bounding cuts inside UTF-8 sequences and UTF-16 surrogate pairs (boundPreview/safeChunks), fabricating U+FFFD and lone surrogates and exceeding maxBytes by up to 2 bytes
description:
Adversarial review finding (flywheel reviewer, run g1-r3) against machine/flywheel/wb-g1g.1 @ 96b64fa (tree 9cd29f2, gate cmd_a8b4e1ffdff4). Reproduced in a detached review worktree at 96b64fa with vitest 4.1.10; probe files were deleted after the run, nothing tracked was modified.

CONFIRMED: src/workbench/evidence-loader.ts bounds preview text by raw UTF-8 bytes and by UTF-16 code units, never by code points, so the bounded preview can contain characters the evidence never contained and can exceed the per-entry byte budget.

1. boundPreview (evidence-loader.ts, `Buffer.from(part).subarray(0, remaining).toString()`): a byte cut inside a multi-byte UTF-8 sequence decodes to U+FFFD. Probe: loader preview ['漢'.repeat(1000)] with bytes 3000, store maxBytes 100 -> loaded entry whose preview content (excluding the '[truncated]' marker) is 102 bytes and whose last content line ends in U+FFFD ('漢'x33 + '�'). Measured: {"sum":113,"withoutMark":102,"maxBytes":100,"hasFFFD":true}. The bead's AC3 says "at most maxBytes per entry"; the overshoot is bounded (at most 2 bytes: a 1-byte partial replaced by a 3-byte U+FFFD) but it is a measured violation, and the U+FFFD is a glyph not present in the source.

2. safeChunks (evidence-loader.ts, `cleaned.slice(at, at + EVIDENCE_LINE_CHARS)`): slicing at 240 UTF-16 code units splits a surrogate pair when the boundary is odd relative to the pairs. Probe: preview ['a' + '😀'.repeat(130)] (261 code units) -> two chunks of lengths [240, 21]; chunk 0 ends with "\ude00\ud83d" (an unpaired high surrogate) and chunk 1 starts with "\ude00\ud83d" (an unpaired low surrogate). Measured: {"loneSurrogatePerLine":[true,true]}. Neither redactWorkbenchText, stripUnsafeText (UNSAFE_TEXT covers C0/C1 and bidi only), the loader's zero-width strip nor safeWorkflowTerminalText removes lone surrogates, so they survive into the EvidenceEntry and, in the Unicode tier, into the inspector's `add()`/`safe()` output (the ASCII tier masks them as '?'). The existing suites only exercise ASCII payloads at the byte boundary ('x'.repeat(1 MiB)) and even-length emoji-free lines, so neither case is pinned; the 107 existing cases pass.

Why it matters (quoted criteria from the bead): AC3 docs/workbench/09 "store reference/short redacted preview" -> "at most maxBytes per entry (preview bounded)"; AC4 docs/workbench/12-security.md § "Input and output hardening": "Validate Unicode and terminal escape sequences before display" and docs/workbench/10 "visible unknowns, never fabricated". A preview that shows U+FFFD or lone surrogates displays text the source never carried; the bounded view should cut on code-point boundaries and keep the byte budget exact.

Suggested fix (evidence-loader.ts only; no hot or do-not-edit file): in boundPreview, accumulate code points (for..of) while Buffer.byteLength(cp) fits `remaining`, never cut inside a sequence; in safeChunks, chunk with Array.from(cleaned) (code points) so a pair is never split; optionally strip any remaining lone surrogate in the loader's own local pass (ruling 8 already gives that pass the zero-width strip). Red-first pins in test/workbench-evidence-loader.test.ts: (a) '漢'.repeat(1000) at maxBytes 100 -> content bytes <= 100 and no U+FFFD in any line; (b) 'a'+'😀'.repeat(130) -> no lone surrogate in any chunk (regex /[\uD800-\uDBFF](?![\uDC00-\uDFFF])|(?<![\uD800-\uDBFF])[\uDC00-\uDFFF]/ matches no line); plus one inspector case rendering (b) at 120x40 Unicode tier with the same assertion over every output line, visibleWidth <= width.

Relation to the open wb-g1g.1 respin (BOUNDARY 09:59:13Z ruling: unauthorized for a missing grant, branch frozen at 96b64fa until the respin lands fast-forward): this is a distinct, additive P3 defect in the same module; the owner may fold it into that respin or land it as a follow-up after wb-g1g.1 closes. Not a duplicate of wb-952 (sanitizer order / zero-width class), wb-563 (host-clock capturedAt) or the redactWorkbenchText non-idempotence P3; store-wide bead search for fffd / multibyte / subarray / byte budget returned nothing.

title: W22-L/docs-16: fork divergence record and census falsifier (docs/16 'Record fork divergence in this documentation': a measured table of pre-existing upstream paths the fork modified since the TRACEABILITY baseline, checked by one vitest diffing baseline..HEAD for upstream-owned src/ and test/ paths; unrecorded divergence fails naming the path, a stale row fails, git or baseline unavailable fails explicitly; red at 250c0af with 17 unrecorded paths); docs/16 table + one test, no src edits
description:
Gap (measured at origin/workbench/implementation-program 250c0af, groom seat g2 round 12): docs/workbench/16-repository-refactor.md section "Upstream maintainability" requires "Record fork divergence in this documentation" and "Keep a focused upstream sync process that checks source changes to runtime, worker, progress, dialog and SDK APIs", and section "Principle" requires "preserve source history/tests/upstream update path". Nothing records or checks the divergence. Measured with `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=M 38034a043e63a65ec5a81544c7a81d0e6b76ebe3..origin/workbench/implementation-program -- src ':!src/workbench' test ':!test/workbench*'` (the baseline is the fork sha TRACEABILITY.md names in its "Baseline:" line; `git cat-file -t` confirms it is a reachable commit): 17 pre-existing upstream paths are modified - src/index.ts, src/settings.ts, src/ui/workflow-card.ts, src/ui/workflow-dialog.ts, src/ui/workflow-menu.ts, src/workflow/host.ts, src/workflow/journal.ts, src/workflow/meta.ts, src/workflow/progress.ts, src/workflow/runtime.ts, src/workflow/saved.ts, src/workflow/task.ts, src/workflow/tool-description.ts, src/workflow/worker-source.ts, test/workflow-meta.test.ts, test/workflow-progress.test.ts, test/workflow-task.test.ts. The docs/16 section "Source-level refactor plan" table names 12 planned paths; it omits src/settings.ts, src/ui/workflow-menu.ts, src/workflow/meta.ts, src/workflow/saved.ts, src/workflow/task.ts, src/workflow/tool-description.ts and the three tests, and still lists src/agent-runner.ts, src/ui/conversation-viewer.ts and src/ui/fleet-list.ts, which are unmodified. The record is stale in both directions and no falsifier exists (bd census: no bead mentions fork divergence, upstream sync or the baseline census; wb-wh7 W01 recorded the baseline only). Newly added files such as src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts are not divergence of an upstream path and are out of this census by construction (--diff-filter=M).

Scope (atomic, test-only plus one docs table; src/ untouched; hot-file free):
- docs/workbench/16-repository-refactor.md gains a section "## Measured fork divergence" holding one table with columns path | recorded at (short sha) | note, listing every pre-existing upstream path the fork has modified. The baseline sha is NOT repeated there: the single carrier stays the TRACEABILITY.md "Baseline:" line, which the test parses (wb-cax.8 single-carrier rule).
- test/workbench-upstream-divergence.test.ts (new): reads the baseline sha from docs/workbench/TRACEABILITY.md, verifies it is a reachable commit (`git cat-file -e <sha>^{commit}`), runs `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=M <sha> HEAD -- src ':!src/workbench' test ':!test/workbench*'` via execFileSync('git', [...]) with cwd at the repository root, parses the docs/16 table, and asserts set equality both ways: a divergent path missing from the table fails naming the path and the sentence to add ("record it in docs/workbench/16 section Measured fork divergence"); a table row whose path no longer differs from the baseline fails as stale; a table row whose path never existed at the baseline fails as misrecorded. When git is unavailable, the repository is not a checkout, or the baseline commit is unreachable (shallow clone), the test FAILS with a message beginning "unknown:" and the reason - it never passes and never silently skips (docs/14 "An omitted test level needs an explicit reason; never imply it ran"). No environment variable disables the check.
- Red: the test fails at 250c0af before the table exists, listing all 17 paths. Green: the table records the 17 measured paths at the recording sha. Falsifier proof: temporarily appending an unrecorded path's modification (in the test's own temp git fixture, not the rig) turns the check red; a stale row turns it red.
- To keep the gate hermetic the test uses the real repository for the measurement AND a small temporary git repository fixture (mkdtemp, `git init`, two commits) for the red/stale falsifiers, so the falsifiers do not depend on mutating the rig.

Out of scope: editing any src/ file; modifying the docs/16 "Source-level refactor plan" table (planned paths stay a plan; the new table is the measured record); the TRACEABILITY validator (wb-cax.1); any hot file (BOUNDARY 40a031a entry plus src/ui/workflow-card.ts); qa/ scripts or forge.toml.

Files: docs/workbench/16-repository-refactor.md (one new section), test/workbench-upstream-divergence.test.ts (new). Specs: docs/workbench/16 (Principle; Upstream maintainability), docs/workbench/14 (Truth labels and release gates), docs/workbench/17 (Release checklist item 1), docs/workbench/TRACEABILITY.md (Baseline line, single carrier of the fork sha).
acceptance_criteria:
Red-first: test/workbench-upstream-divergence.test.ts fails at 250c0af before docs/workbench/16 carries the "Measured fork divergence" table, naming all 17 measured paths. Base 250c0af or later. All quotes are from docs/workbench in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program).

C1. docs/workbench/16-repository-refactor.md section "Upstream maintainability": "Record fork divergence in this documentation." - the new docs/16 table lists every pre-existing upstream path (src/ and test/ outside src/workbench and test/workbench*) modified since the baseline, and the test asserts the table equals the measurement in both directions (unrecorded path fails naming it; stale row fails; misrecorded path fails).
C2. Same section: "Keep a focused upstream sync process that checks source changes to runtime, worker, progress, dialog and SDK APIs." - the measurement is `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=M <baseline> HEAD -- src ':!src/workbench' test ':!test/workbench*'`, so any new edit to an upstream file (runtime, worker, progress, dialog, index, settings, tests) is caught at the candidate's own HEAD until it is recorded.
C3. docs/workbench/16 section "Principle": "Move only enough code to establish correct boundaries; preserve source history/tests/upstream update path." - the census reports modifications only (--diff-filter=M); newly added Workbench files are not counted as upstream divergence, and no src/ file changes in this bead.
C4. docs/workbench/TRACEABILITY.md "Baseline: fork `38034a043e63a65ec5a81544c7a81d0e6b76ebe3`" is the single carrier of the baseline sha: the test parses it and the docs/16 table does not repeat it (wb-cax.8 single-carrier rule); the test verifies the sha is a reachable commit before measuring.
C5. docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md section "Truth labels and release gates": "Each major work package must have a falsifier: a negative test that would fail if a critical guarantee was quietly weakened." and TRACEABILITY "Evidence rules": "An omitted test level needs an explicit reason; never imply it ran." - git unavailable, not a checkout, or unreachable baseline FAILS with a message starting "unknown:" and the reason; there is no environment switch that turns the check into a pass.
C6. docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md section "Release checklist" item 1: "Sources and upstream license preserved; fork origin recorded." - the recorded table names the recording sha per row so the record is dated evidence, not a claim.
C7. Hermetic falsifier proof: the test builds a temporary git repository fixture (mkdtemp, git init, two commits) to prove the unrecorded-path and stale-row failures without mutating the rig; the proposed closure quotes the red run, the green run and the fixture falsifier run.
